question: According to the Chapter Eleven EPSDT table of contents on page 1, on what page is Rule 560-X-11-.07 Screening Schedule listed?

citations.quote: 560-X-11-.07 Screening Schedule 4

question: Within how many days after initial Medicaid eligibility determination must Alabama Medicaid generally inform EPSDT-eligible individuals or their families about the EPSDT program?
answer: Generally within 60 days of the individual's initial Medicaid eligibility determination, and annually thereafter for families which have not utilized EPSDT services.

citations.quote: Generally, this information will be provided within 60 days of the individual's initial Medicaid eligibility determination and in the case of families which have not utilized EPSDT services, annually thereafter.

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-11-.03 Eligibility (1), which persons are eligible for the Alabama Medicaid EPSDT program?
answer: All persons under twenty-one (21) years of age except SOBRA adult eligibles who have been certified as being eligible for Medicaid are eligible for the EPSDT program.

citations.quote: Rule No. 560-X-11-.03 Eligibility (1) All persons under twenty-one (21) years of age except SOBRA adult eligibles who have been certified as being eligible for Medicaid are eligible for the EPSDT program.

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-11-.05 Providers of Screening Services, what must providers of screening services do to participate in the EPSDT Program and what is the exception?
answer: All providers of screening services must enter into an agreement with Alabama Medicaid Agency to participate in the EPSDT Program as a screening provider. Exception: QMB-only providers.

citations.quote: All providers of screening services must enter into an agreement with Alabama Medicaid Agency to participate in the EPSDT Program as a screening provider. Exception: QMB-only providers.

question: How many EPSDT Intensive Developmental Diagnostic Assessments may a recipient receive in a lifetime, and what age group is eligible?
answer: Two per recipient per lifetime, limited to infants 0 to under two years of age.

citations.quote: An EPSDT Intensive Developmental Diagnostic Assessment is a multidisciplinary comprehensive screening limited to infants 0 to under two years of age, and is also limited to two per recipient per lifetime.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid Rule 560-X-11-.10, how are governmental screening providers reimbursed for EPSDT screening?
answer: Governmental screening providers, including physicians, are paid on a negotiated rate basis which will not exceed their actual costs.

citations.quote: Governmental screening providers (including physicians) will be paid on a negotiated rate basis which will not exceed their actual costs.

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-11-.13 State Laboratory Services, which specimens is the State Laboratory arranged to examine?
answer: Blood specimens for sickle cell anemia and other abnormal hemoglobins, stool specimens for ova and parasites, and scotch tape preparations for pinworms.

citations.quote: Rule No. 560-X-11-.13 State Laboratory Services (1) Arrangements have been made with the Clinical Laboratory Administration to have the State Laboratory examine blood specimens for sickle cell anemia and other abnormal hemoglobins, stool specimens for ova and parasites, and scotch tape preparations for pinworms.

question: Which types of providers are listed as EPSDT-only providers under Alabama Medicaid?
answer: Physical therapists, occupational therapists, speech therapists, licensed behavior analysts, chiropractors, podiatrists, psychologists, licensed professional counselors, licensed marriage and family therapists, licensed social workers, private duty nurses, air transportation, environmental lead investigators, and personal care services.

citations.quote: (a) EPSDT-only providers include: physical therapists, occupational therapists, speech therapists, licensed behavior analysts, chiropractors, podiatrists, psychologists, licensed professional counselors, licensed marriage and family therapists, licensed social workers, private duty nurses, air transportation, environmental lead investigators, and personal care services.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid EPSDT rules, how frequently must a licensed physical therapist document and sign supervision visits for care provided by a PT assistant?
answer: Scheduled supervision visits must be documented and signed by the PT at a minimum every 6th visit.

citations.quote: Scheduled visits to supervise care provided by the assistant must be documented and signed by the PT at a minimum every 6th visit.

question: What are the direct supervision requirements for speech-language pathology assistants under Alabama Medicaid EPSDT?
answer: Direct supervision requires the physical presence of the licensed speech pathologist in the same facility at all times when the assistant is performing assigned clinical responsibilities. The licensed speech pathologist must document direct observation of at least ten (10%) percent of all clinical services provided by the assistant, and may supervise no more than the equivalent of two full-time assistants concurrently.

citations.quote: Direct supervision requires the physical presence of the licensed speech pathologist in the same facility at all times when the assistant is performing assigned clinical responsibilities.
The licensed speech pathologist must document direct observation of at least ten (10%) percent of all clinical services provided by the assistant.
Speech therapists may supervise no more than the equivalent of two full-time assistants concurrently.

question: What stage of decubitus ulcers is covered under Secondary Requisites for nursing recipients?
answer: Coverage is for stage three or four ulcers.

citations.quote: (I) Decubitus ulcers – Coverage for stage three or four ulcers.

question: According to the Alabama Medicaid EPSDT administrative code excerpt, what minimum daily duration of mechanical ventilator support is required?
answer: Mechanical ventilator support is necessary for at least six hours per day and appropriate weaning steps are in progress on a continuing basis.

citations.quote: (I) Mechanical ventilator support is necessary for at least six hours per day and appropriate weaning steps are in progress on a continuing basis.

question: For how long may Medicaid continue private duty nursing hours when the qualified primary caregiver is incapacitated due to temporary illness?
answer: Up to 90 days if the qualified primary caregiver is incapacitated due to personal illness or illness of another family member who is dependent upon the caregiver and there is no other trained caregiver available in the home, with medical documentation from the caregiver’s attending physician required.

citations.quote: Private duty nursing hours may be provided for a period up to 90 days if the qualified primary caregiver is incapacitated due to personal illness or illness of another family member who is dependent upon the caregiver and there is no other trained caregiver available in the home.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid EPSDT private duty nursing rules, how is a missed visit defined?
answer: A missed visit occurs when the recipient is at home waiting for scheduled services, but the services are not delivered.

citations.quote: A missed visit occurs when the recipient is at home waiting for scheduled services, but the services are not delivered.

question: Who must employ or contract Personal Care Workers who provide Personal Care Services under the Alabama Medicaid EPSDT rule?
answer: Personal Care Workers must be employed by, or under contract with any enrolled Private Duty Nursing provider.

citations.quote: 2. Personal Care Workers must be employed by, or under contract with any enrolled Private Duty Nursing provider.

question: According to the Chapter Sixteen Pharmaceutical Services Table of Contents, on what page does Rule 560-X-16-.06 Reimbursement for Covered Drugs and Services begin?
answer: Page 7

citations.quote: 560-X-16-.06 Reimbursement for Covered Drugs and Services 7

question: On which page does Rule 560-X-16-.28 Prior Authorization begin according to the table of contents?

citations.quote: 560-X-16-.28 Prior Authorization 21

question: According to Rule No. 560-X-16-.01(4), when is a facsimile acceptable for a Schedule II controlled substance prescription?
answer: Telephone prescriptions are not allowed for Schedule II controlled substances and the pharmacist must obtain an original prescription and maintain that documentation on file, except that for a resident of a long-term care facility a Schedule II prescription may be transmitted by the practitioner or the practitioner’s agent to the dispensing pharmacy by facsimile and the facsimile shall serve as the original written prescription.

citations.quote: Telephone prescriptions are not allowed for Schedule II controlled substances. The pharmacist must obtain an original prescription and maintain that documentation on file.

EXCEPTION: In accordance with Alabama pharmacy law, Controlled Substances Act, §20-2-58(c), a prescription written for Schedule II substances for a resident of a long-term care facility may be transmitted by the practitioner or the agent of the practitioner to the dispensing pharmacy by facsimile. The facsimile shall serve as the original written prescription.

question: What must an Alabama Medicaid pharmacy do if it receives a written outpatient prescription after April 1, 2008 that is not on a tamper-resistant prescription blank?
answer: The pharmacy must contact the prescribing provider and either have the prescription re-submitted in compliant written form or convert the prescription, where otherwise allowable, into verbal, faxed or electronic form.

citations.quote: 1. If a written prescription is received which is not on a tamper- resistant prescription blank, the pharmacy must contact the prescribing provider and either have the prescription re-submitted in compliant written form or convert the prescription, where otherwise allowable, into verbal, faxed or electronic form.

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-16-.02 Requirements for Participation, who bears the expenses if Alabama Medicaid must travel out of state to audit a pharmacy provider's records?
answer: The organization being audited will bear all expenses and costs related to the audit, including, but not limited to, travel and reasonable living expenses.

citations.quote: If, due to the location of the provider's records, Medicaid personnel are required to go out of state for an audit, the organization being audited will bear all expenses and costs related to the audit, including, but not limited to, travel and reasonable living expenses.

question: What distance or travel time requirement must a physician's practice meet to be enrolled as a dispensing drug provider in the Alabama Medicaid Pharmacy Program?
answer: The practice must be located more than 50 miles or 50 minutes from the nearest Medicaid-enrolled pharmacy.

citations.quote: A dispensing physician may be enrolled as a drug provider in the Pharmacy Program only if his practice is located more than 50 miles or 50 minutes from the nearest Medicaid-enrolled pharmacy.

question: How often must a pharmacy using an approved unit dose system submit a Medicaid claim for a given drug for a nursing home recipient, and what quantity can be billed?
answer: Only one claim per drug per recipient each month may be submitted, and only the amount of the prescribed drug actually consumed by the patient may be included.

citations.quote: Each pharmacy using an approved unit dose system must submit only one claim per drug per recipient each month and only the amount of the prescribed drug actually consumed by the patient may be included.

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-16-.06 Reimbursement for Covered Drugs and Services, how is payment for blood clotting factor products calculated?
answer: Payment for blood clotting factor products will be the Average Sales Price (ASP) + 6% plus a professional dispensing fee of $10.64.

citations.quote: Payment for blood clotting factor products will be the Average Sales Price (ASP) + 6% plus a professional dispensing fee of $10.64.

question: What is the maximum Medicaid payment for a facility that purchases drugs through the Federal Supply Schedule?
answer: Payment shall not exceed the entity's actual acquisition cost for the drug, plus a professional dispensing fee of $10.64.

citations.quote: (d) For facilities purchasing drugs through the Federal Supply Schedule (FSS), payment shall not exceed the entity's actual acquisition cost for the drug, plus a professional dispensing fee of $10.64.

question: According to Rule No. 560-X-16-.08, which program has final approval of injectable medications and the reimbursement rate billed by a physician or outpatient hospital?
answer: The Medicaid Pharmacy Program will review and have final approval of injectable medications and the rate of reimbursement billed to the fiscal agent by the physician or outpatient hospital.

citations.quote: The Medicaid Pharmacy Program will review and have final approval of injectable medications and the rate of reimbursement that is billed to the fiscal agent by the physician or outpatient hospital.

question: Which groups or services are exempt from the Medicaid cost-sharing fee under the rule?
answer: The cost-sharing fee does not apply to family planning drugs and supplies, drugs prescribed for recipients under 18 years of age, recipients who are in a nursing facility, or services furnished to pregnant women.

citations.quote: (2) The cost-sharing fee does not apply to family planning drugs and supplies, or to drugs prescribed for recipients under 18 years of age, recipients who are in a nursing facility or services furnished to pregnant women.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid Rule No. 560-X-16-.12 Over-the-Counter Medications, what is required for over-the-counter medications/products?
answer: Over-the-counter medications/products require a signed prescription from a physician or other practitioner legally licensed by the State of Alabama to prescribe the drugs authorized under the program.

citations.quote: Over-the-counter medications/products require a signed prescription from a physician or other practitioner legally licensed by the State of Alabama to prescribe the drugs authorized under the program.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid Rule No. 560-X-16-.20, what is the maximum number of refills allowed for a non-controlled prescription and what happens to claims beyond that limit?
answer: A prescription for a non-controlled drug may not exceed a maximum of eleven refills. Claims for prescription refills beyond eleven refills for non-controlled prescriptions shall be denied.

citations.quote: The quantity for which a prescription is written should not exceed a maximum of eleven refills for non-controlled prescriptions or five refills for Control III-V prescriptions. Claims for prescription refills beyond eleven refills for non-controlled prescriptions or five refills for Control III-V prescriptions shall be denied.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid Rule No. 560-X-16-.21 Prescription Refill, what is the maximum number of refills authorized for non-controlled prescriptions and for Schedule III-V controlled prescriptions?
answer: Prescriptions will have a maximum of no more than eleven (11) refills for non controlled prescriptions or five (5) refills for Control III-V prescriptions authorized.

citations.quote: Rule No. 560-X-16-.21 Prescription Refill (1) Prescriptions will have a maximum of no more than eleven (11) refills for non controlled prescriptions or five (5) refills for Control III-V prescriptions authorized.

question: How many practicing physicians must serve on the Alabama Medicaid DUR Board?
answer: Four practicing physicians.

citations.quote: Board membership shall be composed of four practicing physicians, four practicing pharmacists, two representatives from the state's pharmacy schools, two representatives from the state's medical schools, and two representatives from the Alabama Medicaid Agency

question: According to Rule No. 560-X-16-.24, what three components must Prospective DUR include before each prescription is filled or delivered to a Medicaid recipient?
answer: Screening, patient counseling, and patient profiles.

citations.quote: Prospective DUR (PRODUR) is required at the point of sale or distribution before each prescription is filled or delivered to a Medicaid recipient. It must include screening, patient counseling, and patient profiles.

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-16-.25 Retrospective DUR, where are cases of possible fraud and/or abuse referred?
answer: Cases of possible fraud and/or abuse shall be referred to the Medicaid Program Integrity Division.

citations.quote: Cases of possible fraud and/or abuse shall be referred to the Medicaid Program Integrity Division.

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-16-.27 Preferred Drug List, what is required for a prescription for a drug within the scope of the Medicaid preferred drug list but not included on the preferred drug list to be reimbursed?
answer: Prior authorization is required before reimbursement.

citations.quote: Rule No. 560-X-16-.27 Preferred Drug List (1) The Alabama Medicaid Agency will utilize a preferred drug list for determination of drugs available for reimbursement under the Medicaid Program. Prescriptions for drugs within the scope of the Medicaid preferred drug list that are not included on the preferred drug list require prior authorization before being reimbursed.

question: Under the presentation rules on page 23, what is the consequence of addressing cost information during a presentation?
answer: No cost information can be addressed. Inclusion of cost information will terminate the presentation.

citations.quote: No cost information can be addressed. Inclusion of cost information will terminate the presentation.

question: Who must initiate requests for prior authorization when deemed medically necessary under the Alabama Medicaid Pharmaceutical Services provisions?
answer: The practitioner must initiate requests for prior authorization when deemed medically necessary.

citations.quote: (7) Requests for prior authorization must be initiated by the practitioner when deemed medically necessary.

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-16-.29 Annual Report, what cost information must the annual report to the Secretary of Health and Human Services identify?
answer: The report must include an estimate of the cost savings generated as a result of the DUR program and must identify costs of DUR and savings to the Medicaid drug program attributable to prospective and retrospective DUR.

citations.quote: (j) An estimate of the cost savings generated as a result of the DUR program. This report must identify costs of DUR and savings to the Medicaid drug program attributable to prospective and retrospective DUR.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid Rule No. 560-X-16-.31 Hemophilia Management Standards of Care, what minimum emergency support must a provider agree to provide to be paid for providing blood clotting factor to recipients?
answer: Emergency telephone support 24 hours a day, 7 days a week to ensure patients are directed appropriately for care in emergent situations.

citations.quote: (4) Emergency telephone support 24 hours a day, 7 days a week to ensure patients are directed appropriately for care in emergent situations.

question: What are the minimum annual continuing education hour requirements for pharmacists versus nurses and social workers for hemophilia or related blood clotting factor-related diseases under the cited provision?
answer: Pharmacists are required to obtain a minimum of 2 Continuing Education (CE, CME or CEU) credit hours per year that are specific to hemophilia or related blood clotting factor-related diseases. Nurses and social workers are required to obtain a minimum of 4 Continuing Education (CEU) hours per year that are specific to hemophilia or related blood clotting factor-related diseases. Continuing education must be specific to hemophilia or related blood clotting factor-related diseases and must be recognized by a state or national health care professional accrediting body.

citations.quote: (a) Pharmacists are required to obtain a minimum of 2 Continuing Education (CE, CME or CEU) credit hours per year that are specific to hemophilia or related blood clotting factor-related diseases. (b) Nurses and social workers are required to obtain a minimum of 4 Continuing Education (CEU) hours per year that are specific to hemophilia or related blood clotting factor-related diseases. Continuing education must be specific to hemophilia or related blood clotting factor-related diseases and must be recognized by a state or national health care professional accrediting body.

question: What must a provider do upon discontinuation of hemophilia-related services?
answer: The provider must coordinate for another designated health care provider to provide services prior to withdrawal of hemophilia-related services from the home, continue to provide services and supplies until the individual obtains an alternate source, and make every effort including notification to the Medicaid Director of Pharmacy to find an alternative provider.

citations.quote: Upon discontinuation of services by the provider, the provider shall, at a minimum, coordinate for another designated health care provider to provide services to covered persons, prior to withdrawal of any hemophilia-related services from the home of any covered person.
The provider shall continue to provide services and supplies to a covered individual until the individual obtains an alternate source of services and supplies.

Every effort shall be made by the provider (including notification to the Medicaid Director of Pharmacy) to find an alternative provider to ensure that the coordination of care/transition follows the minimum standards of care as set forth in this document.

question: According to the Chapter Ten Long Term Care table of contents, on which page does Rule 560-X-10-.14 Resident Rights begin?
answer: Page 16

citations.quote: 560-X-10-.14 Resident Rights 16

question: According to the table of contents on page 2, on what page does Rule 560-X-10-.18 Availability of Nursing Facilities Accounting Records begin?

citations.quote: 560-X-10-.18 Availability of Nursing Facilities Accounting Records 23

question: Under Alabama Medicaid Chapter 10 Rule No. 560-X-10-.01(1), what is the age exception to the prohibition on a nursing facility including an institution for the care and treatment of mental disease?
answer: A nursing facility may not include an institution for the care and treatment of mental disease except for services furnished to individuals age 65 and over.

citations.quote: A facility may not include any institution that is for the care and treatment of mental disease except for services furnished to individuals age 65 and over.

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-10-.03 Enrollment and Participation, what requirements must a nursing facility meet to enroll and participate in the Alabama Title XIX Medicaid nursing facility program?
answer: The facility must possess certification for Medicare Title XVIII, submit a budget to the Alabama Medicaid Agency Provider Reimbursement Division for the purpose of establishing a per diem rate, execute a Provider Agreement with Medicaid, and execute a Nursing Facility/Resident Agreement with Medicaid residents.

citations.quote: Rule No. 560-X-10-.03 Enrollment and Participation (1) All nursing facilities that desire to enroll and participate in the Alabama Title XIX Medicaid nursing facility program and to receive Medicaid payment for services provided for Medicaid residents must meet the following requirements: (a) Possess certification for Medicare Title XVIII. (b) Submit a budget to the Alabama Medicaid Agency Provider Reimbursement Division for the purpose of establishing a per diem rate. (2) Execute a Provider Agreement with Medicaid. (3) Execute a Nursing Facility/Resident Agreement with Medicaid residents.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid long-term care rules, what brand requirement applies to covered medically necessary over-the-counter non-legend drug products ordered by a physician?
answer: Medically necessary over-the-counter non-legend drug products ordered by a physician are covered, except over-the-counter insulin covered under the Pharmacy program, and generic brands are required unless brand name is specified in writing by the attending physician.

citations.quote: (i) Medically necessary over-the-counter (non-legend) drug products ordered by a physician, with the exception of over-the-counter insulin covered under the Pharmacy program. Generic brands are required unless brand name is specified in writing by the attending physician.

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-10-.05 Reservation of Beds, how many days of bed reservation may not be charged to a Medicaid patient, their family, or sponsor during a temporary hospital absence?
answer: The first four days of bed reservation during a period in which a Medicaid patient is temporarily absent due to admission to a hospital may not be charged to the Medicaid patient, their family, or their sponsor.

citations.quote: Neither Medicaid patients, nor their families, nor their sponsor, may be charged for reservation of a bed for the first four days of any period during which a Medicaid patient is temporarily absent due to admission to a hospital.

question: When a hospital notifies a nursing facility that a resident is ready for release within the four-day bed-hold period, under what condition must the facility allow the resident to return before the bed-hold expires?
answer: The nursing facility must allow the resident to return before the bed-hold period expires provided the resident is an appropriate placement for nursing facility care and the nursing facility provides the type of services that meets the needs of the resident.

citations.quote: When a nursing facility is contacted by the hospital notifying them that the resident is ready for release, within the four day bed-hold period, the nursing facility must allow the resident to return to their facility before the bed-hold period expires provided the resident is an appropriate placement for nursing facility care and the nursing facility provides the type of services that meets the needs of the resident.

question: What is the maximum therapeutic leave payment limit for nursing facilities per calendar quarter and per visit under Rule 560-X-10-.06?
answer: Payments may be made for up to six days per calendar quarter, and a therapeutic leave visit may not exceed three days; visits may not be combined to exceed the three day limit.

citations.quote: Payments to nursing facilities may be made for therapeutic leave visits to home, relatives, and friends for up to six days per calendar quarter. A therapeutic leave visit may not exceed three days. Visits may not be combined to exceed the three day limit.

question: For residents who are dually eligible for Medicaid and Medicare, what must nursing facilities do first for covered therapy services?
answer: Nursing facilities must first bill Medicare Part A and/or Part B for covered therapy services — including physical therapy, occupational therapy, and speech-language pathology therapy — and fully utilize Medicare coverage so the therapy charge apportionment is accurately captured on the Medicaid cost report.

citations.quote: For residents who are dually eligible for Medicaid and Medicare coverage, nursing facilities must first bill Medicare Part A and/or Part B for covered therapy services – including physical therapy, occupational therapy, and speech-language pathology therapy. Medicare coverage must be fully utilized so that the therapy charge apportionment is accurately captured on the Medicaid cost report.

question: According to the Alabama Medicaid Administrative Code excerpt on page 12, label 10, what is stated about the need for a mobility aid in meeting the Mobility ADL assistance requirement under (k)?
answer: The need for a wheelchair, walker, crutch, cane, or other mobility aid shall not by itself be considered to meet this requirement. Mobility requires physical assistance from another person for mobility on an ongoing basis daily or multiple times per week.

citations.quote: Mobility - The individual requires physical assistance from another person for mobility on an ongoing basis (daily or multiple times per week). Mobility is defined as the ability to walk, using mobility aids such as a walker, crutch, or cane if required, or the ability to use a wheelchair if walking is not feasible. The need for a wheelchair, walker, crutch, cane, or other mobility aid shall not by itself be considered to meet this requirement.

question: Can criterion (a) and criterion (k)(7) both be used as two qualifying criteria for admission to a certified nursing facility under the Skilled Nursing or Rehabilitative Services rule?
answer: No. Only one may be used because both involve medication administration. If an individual meets criterion (a), criterion (k)(7) may not be used as the second qualifying criterion.

citations.quote: Criterion (a) and Criterion (k) (7) are the same as they both involve medication administration. Only one may be used. Therefore, if an individual meets criterion (a), criterion (k) (7) may not be used as the second qualifying criterion.

question: Under Rule 560-X-10-.11 Application of Medicare Coverage, when may a nursing facility apply for Medicaid eligibility for a resident who may be Medicare eligible?
answer: A nursing facility must apply for eligible Medicare coverage prior to Medicaid coverage and cannot apply for Medicaid eligibility for a resident until Medicare coverage is discontinued.

citations.quote: (b) Nursing facilities must apply for eligible Medicare coverage prior to Medicaid coverage.
(c) Nursing facilities cannot apply for Medicaid eligibility for a resident until Medicare coverage is discontinued.

question: For Medicaid retrospective reviews, what documents must all Medicaid certified ICF/IID facilities complete and maintain in their files for new admissions?
answer: A fully completed Medicaid Patient Status Notification (Form 199), a fully completed ICF/IID Level of Care Evaluation for Institutional Care (Form 361), the resident’s physical history, the resident’s psychological history, the resident’s interim rehabilitation plan, and a social evaluation of the resident.

citations.quote: (d) All Medicaid certified ICF/ IID facilities are required to complete and maintain the following documents in their files for Medicaid retrospective reviews. These documents support the ICF/IID level of care needs. 1. New Admissions (i) A fully completed Medicaid Patient Status Notification (Form 199). (ii) A fully completed ICF/IID Level of Care Evaluation for Institutional Care (Form 361). (iii) The resident’s physical history. (iv) The resident’s psychological history. (v) The resident’s interim rehabilitation plan. (vi) A social evaluation of the resident.

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-10-.12 Utilization Review for ICF/IID, what utilization review requirements must an ICF/IID comply with?
answer: An ICF/IID must comply with the utilization review requirements contained in 42 C.F.R. §§456.350-456.438.

citations.quote: Rule No. 560-X-10-.12 Utilization Review for ICF/IID (1) An ICF/IID must comply with the utilization review requirements contained in 42 C.F.R. §§456.350-456.438 (“Utilization Review Requirements”).

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-10-.14 Resident Rights, when and how must a facility notify a resident of his or her rights and services?
answer: The facility must inform the resident both orally and in writing in a language the resident understands of his or her rights and all rules and regulations governing resident conduct and responsibilities during the stay. Such notification must be made prior to or upon admission and during the resident's stay.

citations.quote: The facility must inform the resident both orally and in writing in a language that the resident understands of his or her rights and all rules and regulations governing resident conduct and responsibilities during the stay in the facility. Such notification must be made prior to or upon admission and during the resident's stay.

question: Under the resident rights provisions, what notice must a resident give to inspect and purchase photocopies of all records pertaining to the resident?
answer: The resident must make a written request and give 48 hours’ notice to the facility.

citations.quote: (b) The resident has the right to inspect and purchase photocopies of all records pertaining to the resident, upon written request and 48 hours’ notice to the facility.

question: Under Protection of resident funds, how must a facility deposit a resident's personal funds that exceed $50?
answer: The facility must deposit any resident's personal funds in excess of $50 in an interest bearing account or accounts that is separate from any of the facility's operating accounts, and that credits all interest earned on the resident's account to his or her account.

citations.quote: The facility must deposit any resident's personal funds in excess of $50 in an interest bearing account (or accounts) that is separate from any of the facility's operating accounts, and that credits all interest earned on the resident's account to his or her account.

question: What mail privacy rights does a resident have under (9) Mail?
answer: The resident has the right to privacy in written communications, including the right to send and receive mail promptly that is unopened, and to have access to stationery, postage and writing implements at the resident's own expense.

citations.quote: (9) Mail. The resident has the right to privacy in written communications, including the right to: (a) Send and receive mail promptly that is unopened; and (b) Have access to stationery, postage and writing implements at the resident's own expense.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid LTC rules, when may a resident be prohibited from self-administering drugs?
answer: Each resident has the right to self-administer drugs unless the interdisciplinary team, as defined by 42 C.F.R. Section 483.20(d)(2)(ii), has determined for that resident that this practice is unsafe.

citations.quote: (14) Self-Administration of Drugs. Each resident has the right to self-administer drugs unless the interdisciplinary team, as defined by 42 C.F.R. Section 483.20(d)(2)(ii), has determined for each resident that this practice is unsafe.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid PASRR requirements, what is the consequence if a nursing facility fails to obtain the Level I screening, Level I Determination and Level II Determination, if applicable, made by the Department of Mental Health prior to admitting the resident?
answer: The Alabama Medicaid Agency will recoup all Medicaid payments for nursing facility services from the date of the resident’s admission and continuing until the Level I Determination or Level II Determination, if applicable, is received.

citations.quote: If the nursing facility fails to obtain the Level I screening, Level I Determination and Level II Determination, if applicable, made by the Department of Mental Health prior to admitting the resident into their facility, the Alabama Medicaid Agency will recoup all Medicaid payments for nursing facility services from the date of the resident’s admission and continuing until the Level I Determination or Level II Determination, if applicable, is received.

question: According to the Alabama Medicaid Administrative Code excerpt, what does Alabama law prohibit regarding medication administration in a facility?
answer: Alabama law prohibits nonlicensed personnel from administering medication.

citations.quote: Alabama law prohibits nonlicensed personnel from administering medication.

question: Under Rule 560-X-10-.20, what patient percentage threshold causes a nursing facility to be deemed maintained primarily for the care and treatment of individuals with mental disease?
answer: More than fifty percent (50%) of the patients are receiving care because of disability in functioning resulting from a mental disease.

citations.quote: More than fifty percent (50%) of the patients are receiving care because of disability in functioning resulting from a mental disease.
Rule 560-X-10-.20 Conditions Under Which Nursing Facilities are Not Classified as Mental Disease Facility Under Title XIX

question: According to Rule No. 560-X-10-.23, what action will the Agency take if the 14-day assessment schedule requirements in 42 C.F.R. §483.20 are not met?
answer: The Agency will recoup claims.

citations.quote: The Agency will recoup claims if the 14-day schedule requirements in 42 C.F.R.§ 483.20 are not met.

question: According to Rule No. 560-X-10-.26(1)(a), what is the definition of discharge?
answer: Discharge means movement from an entity that participates in Medicare as a skilled nursing facility (SNF), a Medicare certified distinct part, an entity that participates in Medicaid as a nursing facility (NF), or a Medicaid certified distinct part to a noninstitutional setting when the discharging facility ceases to be legally responsible for the care of the resident.

citations.quote: (a) Discharge means movement from an entity that participates in Medicare as a skilled nursing facility (SNF), a Medicare certified distinct part, an entity that participates in Medicaid as a nursing facility (NF), or a Medicaid certified distinct part to a noninstitutional setting when the discharging facility ceases to be legally responsible for the care of the resident.

question: What must the written notice of transfer or discharge for nursing facilities include regarding the resident's right to appeal to the Alabama Medicaid Agency?
answer: The notice must include the name, mailing address, e-mail address, and telephone number of the Alabama Medicaid Agency and a statement that the resident has the right to appeal the action to the Medicaid Agency by filing a written request within 30 days of the notice of transfer or discharge.

citations.quote: (d) The name, mailing address, e-mail address, and telephone number of the Alabama Medicaid Agency and a statement that the resident has the right to appeal the action to the Medicaid Agency by filing a written request within 30 days of the notice of transfer or discharge;

question: How many days does a resident have to submit a written request for Medicaid review of a transfer or discharge decision?
answer: 30 days from the date of the notice of transfer or discharge.

citations.quote: A resident who is aggrieved by a facility's decision to transfer or discharge the resident may request a review of the decision by the Medicaid Agency. Such request must be in writing and received within 30 days of the date of the notice of transfer or discharge.

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-10-.27 Enforcement of Compliance for Long-Term Care Facilities with Deficiencies, what is the cost to obtain copies of the adopted CMS regulations from Medicaid?
answer: Copies of the adopted CMS regulations are available from Medicaid at a cost of $2.50.

citations.quote: Copies are also available from Medicaid at a cost of $2.50.

question: According to the Chapter Twelve Home Health table of contents, which rule number addresses Billing of Medicaid Recipients by Providers?

citations.quote: 560-X-12-.11 Billing of Medicaid Recipients by Providers 6

question: According to Rule No. 560-X-12-.01 Home Health Care - General, who may refer a person for Alabama Medicaid Home Health Care?
answer: Anyone may refer a person who is in need of home health care, under the care of a physician, and in need of part-time nursing, to a participating agency.

citations.quote: (2) Anyone may refer a person who is in need of home health care, under the care of a physician, and in need of part-time nursing, to a participating agency.

question: What advance written notice must a participating home health agency give to Alabama Medicaid to withdraw from the program?
answer: At least thirty (30) days in advance.

citations.quote: (1) A participating agency has the right to withdraw from the Medicaid program after giving written notice to Medicaid of its intent at least thirty (30) days in advance.

question: Are RN supervisory visits to evaluate appropriateness of services provided by an LPN, home health aide, or orderly billable as skilled nursing services under Alabama Medicaid Home Health Care?
answer: No. Supervisory visits made by a professional registered nurse to evaluate appropriateness of services being rendered to a patient by an LPN, home health aide, or orderly are considered administrative costs to the agency and may not be billed as skilled nursing services.

citations.quote: Supervisory visits made by a professional registered nurse to evaluate appropriateness of services being rendered to a patient by an LPN, home health aide, or orderly are considered as administrative costs to the agency and may not be billed as skilled nursing services.

question: How often must the ordering physician or NPP recertify care if home health services continue to be necessary?
answer: The ordering physician or NPP must recertify care every sixty (60) days if home health services continue to be necessary.

citations.quote: The ordering physician or NPP must recertify care every sixty (60) days if home health services continue to be necessary.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid Rule No. 560-X-12-.11, may a contracted Home Health Agency bill a Medicaid recipient additional charges for covered home health services?
answer: No. The Home Health Agency agrees to accept as payment in full the amount paid for covered home health services and cannot make any additional charges to the recipient, sponsor, or family of the recipient.

citations.quote: The Home Health Agency agrees to accept as payment in full the amount paid for covered home health services, and cannot make any additional charges to the recipient, sponsor, or family of the recipient.

question: According to the Chapter Thirteen table of contents, on what page does rule 560-X-13-.17 Wheelchairs begin?

citations.quote: 560-X-13-.17 Wheelchairs 12

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-13-.01, how is long-term use defined for Medicaid purchase coverage of DME?
answer: Long term use is defined as the use of DME which exceeds six months, and Medicaid covers the purchase of DME items for long term use.

citations.quote: (a) Medicaid covers the purchase of DME items for long term use. Long term use is defined as the use of DME which exceeds six months.

question: How far in advance of the start of services must the required face-to-face visit for the initial written prescription or order for certain medical supplies, equipment, and appliances occur, and what must it relate to?
answer: The required face-to-face visit must be related to the primary reason why the recipients require the certain medical supplies, equipment, and appliances and must occur no more than 6 months prior to the start of services.

citations.quote: The required face-to-face visit for the initial written prescription or order for certain medical supplies, equipment, and appliances must be related to the primary reason why the recipients require the certain medical supplies, equipment, and appliances and must occur no more than 6 months prior to the start of services.

question: How many days before a surety bond's termination date must Alabama Medicaid DME, supply, appliance, and POP providers submit proof of renewal to the fiscal agent?
answer: At least 30 days prior to the individual bond's termination date.

citations.quote: Proof of the renewal must be submitted to Medicaid’s fiscal agent at least 30 days prior to the individual bond’s termination date.

question: Which provider types are exempt from the minimum 30 hours per week open-to-public requirement in Chapter 13?
answer: Physicians, physical and occupational therapists, and a provider working with custom made orthotics and prosthetics are exempt from the minimum 30 hours per week open-to-public requirement.

citations.quote: All providers mentioned in this chapter must remain open to the public for a minimum of 30 hours per week during normal business hours except physicians, physical and occupational therapists or a provider working with custom made orthotics and prosthetics.

question: Within how many calendar days after DME equipment is dispensed must a prior authorization request be received by the Medicaid fiscal agent?
answer: All prior authorization requests for DME must be received within 30 calendar days after equipment is dispensed; requests received beyond 30 calendar days after equipment is dispensed will be denied.

citations.quote: All prior authorization requests for DME must be received by the Medicaid fiscal agent within 30 calendar days after equipment is dispensed. All prior authorization requests received beyond the 30 calendar days after equipment is dispensed will be denied.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid DME rules, when must a provider submit an extension request for dispensing approved medical items?
answer: An extension may be requested with written justification for why the equipment cannot be supplied timely, and all requests for extensions must be submitted to Medicaid prior to the expiration date indicated on the approval letter.

citations.quote: When a provider is unable to dispense equipment within the timeframe specified on the approval letter, an extension may be requested with written justification as to the specific reason(s) why the equipment cannot be supplied timely. All requests for extensions must be submitted to Medicaid prior to the expiration date indicated on the approval letter.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid Rule 560-X-13-.07, are DME items for use in nursing homes or other institutions covered for children?
answer: Items for use in hospitals, nursing homes, or other institutions are non-covered, but DME items may be provided in nursing homes or other institutions for children through the EPSDT Program.

citations.quote: Rule No. 560-X-13-.07 Non-covered Items and Services Non-covered items and services include, but are not limited to: (3) Items for use in hospitals, nursing homes, or other institutions. However, DME items may be provided in nursing homes or other institutions for children through the EPSDT Program.

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-13-.12 Cost-Sharing, may a provider deny services to an eligible recipient who cannot pay the cost-sharing amount?
answer: No. A provider may not deny services to any eligible recipient due to the recipient's inability to pay the cost-sharing amount imposed.

citations.quote: A provider may not deny services to any eligible recipient due to the recipient's inability to pay the cost-sharing amount imposed.

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-13-.15, is prior authorization required for oxygen therapy coverage?
answer: Yes. Oxygen therapy is covered for the entire Medicaid population based on medical necessity and must be prior authorized by Medicaid.

citations.quote: Oxygen Therapy is covered for the entire Medicaid population based on medical necessity and must be prior authorized by Medicaid.

question: How often may Medicaid approve one manual or power/motorized wheelchair based on medical necessity?
answer: Patients may be approved for one manual or power/motorized wheelchair every five years for children ages 0-20 and every seven years for adults ages 21-99 based on medical necessity.

citations.quote: Patients may be approved for one manual or power/motorized wheelchair every five years for children ages 0-20 and every seven years for adults ages 21-99 based on medical necessity.

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-13-.18, what is the maximum age for Medicaid coverage of basic level prosthetics, orthotics, and pedorthics?
answer: Basic level prosthetics, orthotics and pedorthics are covered benefits to Medicaid eligible recipients up to age 65 in a non-institutional and institutional setting.

citations.quote: Basic level prosthetics, orthotics and pedorthics are covered benefits to Medicaid eligible recipients up to age 65 in a non-institutional and institutional setting.

question: Where must requests for repair or replacement of Medicaid-covered DME items due to extenuating circumstances be mailed?
answer: Alabama Medicaid Agency, 501 Dexter Ave., DME Unit, Montgomery, AL 36103

citations.quote: Request for repair or replacement due to extenuating circumstances should be mailed to, Alabama Medicaid Agency, 501 Dexter Ave., DME Unit, Montgomery, AL 36103.

question: According to the Chapter Fourteen Family Planning table of contents, on what page does Rule 560-X-14-.04 Sterilizations begin?

citations.quote: 560-X-14-.04 Sterilizations 3

question: According to Alabama Medicaid Chapter 14 Rule No. 560-X-14-.01, what type of consent is required prior to a face-to-face family planning encounter?
answer: Written consent is required.

citations.quote: Individuals are required to give written or verbal consent prior to receiving family planning services.
For any face-to-face encounter a written consent is required.

question: How many Periodic Revisit visits are allowed per calendar year under Alabama Medicaid Family Planning?
answer: No more than four revisits per calendar year.

citations.quote: (c) Periodic Revisit - a follow-up evaluation of a new or existing family planning condition. Services include a review with update of history, a review of the effectiveness of current contraceptive method with counseling regarding any existing problems and adjustment of contraceptive method to include issuance of supplies as indicated. This visit includes scheduled follow-up, as medically indicated, of chosen birth control method. Limited to no more than four (4) revisits per calendar year.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid Rule No. 560-X-14-.04, what minimum age must an individual meet at the time sterilization consent is obtained?
answer: The individual must be at least twenty-one (21) years old at the time consent is obtained.

citations.quote: (a) The individual is at least twenty-one (21) years old at the time consent is obtained;

question: Is removal of contraceptive implants due to medical complications considered a family planning service under Alabama Medicaid?
answer: No. Removal of contraceptive implants due to medical complications are not family planning services; however, the removal may be covered as a medical service through the Physician's Program.

citations.quote: (9) Removal of contraceptive implants due to medical complications are not family planning services; however, the removal may be covered as a medical service through the Physician's Program.

question: What family income limit and disregard applies for eligibility for Alabama Family Planning Services?
answer: Family income must be at or below 141% of the federal poverty level. A standard income disregard of 5% of the federal poverty level is applied if the individual is not eligible for coverage due to excess income.

citations.quote: Have family income at or below 141% of the federal poverty level. A standard income disregard of 5% of the federal poverty level is applied if the individual is not eligible for coverage due to excess income

question: What income condition terminates Alabama Family Planning eligibility?
answer: Coverage terminates when the recipient’s gross countable family income exceeds 141% of the FPL. A standard income disregard of 5% of the FPL is applied if the individual is not eligible for coverage due to excess income.

citations.quote: (a) The recipient’s gross countable family income exceeds 141% of the FPL. A standard income disregard of 5% of the FPL is applied if the individual is not eligible for coverage due to excess income

question: Are Medicaid recipients required to pay co-payments for family planning prescription drugs and refills under Rule 560-X-14-.08?
answer: No. Co-payment on prescription drugs and any indicated refills does not apply to drugs and supplies designated as family planning items.

citations.quote: The co-payment on prescription drugs, and any indicated refills for Medicaid recipients does not apply to drugs and supplies designated as family planning items.

question: According to Rule No. 560-X-14-.11 on page 10, what is provided to each enrolled family planning provider and what may happen if providers do not follow the procedures outlined?
answer: The Alabama Medicaid Provider Manual, including Appendix C which details the elements of each family planning visit, instructions for completion of forms, and procedures to follow in the administration of the local program, is provided to each enrolled provider. Family planning providers will be required to follow procedures outlined in the manual, and failure to do so may result in the recoupment of claims paid to the provider.

citations.quote: (1) The Alabama Medicaid Provider Manual, including Appendix C, which details the elements of each family planning visit, instructions for completion of forms, and procedures to follow in the administration of the local program, is provided to each enrolled provider.
(2) Family planning providers will be required to follow procedures outlined in the manual. Failure to do so may result in the recoupment of claims paid to the provider.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid Chapter 15 Rule No. 560-X-15-.01, what dental services availability is required for eligible children under age 21?
answer: The availability of certain dental health care services for eligible children under age 21 is required through the Alabama Medicaid Program as part of the Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnosis, and Treatment (EPSDT) Program.

citations.quote: (a) The availability of certain dental health care services for eligible children under age 21 is required through the Alabama Medicaid Program as part of the Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnosis, and Treatment (EPSDT) Program.

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-15-.03 Limitations, which Medicaid eligible individuals are provided dental care?
answer: Dental care is provided to Medicaid eligible individuals who are under age 21 and are eligible for treatment under the EPSDT Program.

citations.quote: Dental care is provided to Medicaid eligible individuals who are under age 21 and are eligible for treatment under the EPSDT Program.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid dental policy, what is the lifetime limit for dental sealant applications per tooth?
answer: One application per tooth in a recipient's lifetime.

citations.quote: (5) Dental sealants are covered by Medicaid, and are limited to one application per tooth in a recipient's lifetime.

question: According to Rule No. 560-X-15-.06(1), where can a dental provider download an enrollment application?
answer: From the Medicaid website at www.medicaid.alabama.gov.

citations.quote: An enrollment application may be requested from the Medicaid fiscal agent or downloaded from the Medicaid website at www.medicaid.alabama.gov.

question: What signature is required on the Mobile Dental Clinic consent form?
answer: The consent form shall require the signature of a parent or legal guardian.

citations.quote: (d) The consent form shall require the signature of a parent or legal guardian.

question: Within what radius must a Mobile Dental Clinic arrange emergency follow-up care with a permanently established dental facility?
answer: Within a 50-mile radius of where mobile services are provided.

citations.quote: The operator shall maintain a written procedure for emergency follow-up care for patients treated in a Mobile Dental Clinic, which includes arrangements for treatment and follow-up care by a qualified dentist in a dental facility that is permanently established within a 50-mile radius of where mobile services are provided.

question: On what date did the new rule become effective according to the history on page 9?
answer: September 15, 2008

citations.quote: History: New Rule: Filed June 20, 2008; effective September 15, 2008.

question: According to the Chapter Seventeen Eye Care Services Table of Contents, what is the rule title for 560-X-17-.04?
answer: Eyeglasses

citations.quote: 560-X-17-.04 Eyeglasses 3

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-17-.01(1) Eye Care Services - General, which eye care providers are eligible to participate in the Alabama Medicaid Program?
answer: Only in-state and borderline out-of-state eye care services providers within a 30-mile radius of the state line who meet enrollment requirements are eligible to participate.

citations.quote: Only in-state and borderline out-of-state eye care services providers (within a 30-mile radius of the state line) who meet enrollment requirements are eligible to participate in the Alabama Medicaid Program.

question: How often are Medicaid recipients twenty-one years of age and older authorized a complete eye examination and work-up?
answer: Recipients twenty-one years of age and older are authorized one complete eye examination and work-up every two calendar years.

citations.quote: (c) Medicaid recipients twenty-one (21) years of age and older are authorized one (1) complete eye examination and work-up every two (2) calendar years; recipients under twenty-one (21) years of age are authorized two (2) complete eye examinations and work-ups every calendar year or more often if medical necessity is documented.

question: What is the maximum amount Medicaid will pay for eyeglasses procured from a non-central source?
answer: Medicaid will pay no more than the contract price charged by the central source.

citations.quote: At the option of the provider making the frame measurements, eyeglasses in conformance with Medicaid standards, may be procured from either the central Medicaid source or from any other source. Medicaid will pay no more than the contract price charged by the central source.

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-17-.05 Billing Procedures, within what timeframe must claims for eye care services be forwarded to the Medicaid fiscal agent for payment?
answer: Claims are to be forwarded directly to the Medicaid fiscal agent for payment within one year of the date of service.

citations.quote: Claims are to be forwarded directly to the Medicaid fiscal agent for payment within one year of the date of service.

question: When eyeglasses are procured from the central Medicaid source contractor, how must fitting claims be submitted?
answer: The claims are to be sent for payment directly to the Medicaid fiscal agent and the claim will specify the fitting services only.

citations.quote: (8) Fitting (Including Frame Service, Verification, and Subsequent Service) only, when eyeglasses are procured from the central Medicaid source contractor: (a) The claims are to be sent for payment directly to the Medicaid fiscal agent. (b) The claim will specify the fitting services only.

question: On what page of Chapter Eighteen is Rule 560-X-18-.03 Prior Authorization listed in the Table of Contents?
answer: Page 2

citations.quote: 560-X-18-.03 Prior Authorization 2

question: According to the Chapter 18 Transportation Services table of contents on page 2, on which page is rule 560-X-18-.19 Administration of the NET Program listed?

citations.quote: 560-X-18-.19 Administration of the NET Program 10

question: According to Rule No. 560-X-18-.02 Definitions, what three levels of ambulance services does Alabama Medicaid recognize?
answer: Basic Life Support (BLS), Advanced Life Support (ALS), and Non-emergency Ambulance Transportation.

citations.quote: Medicaid recognizes three levels of ambulance services: Basic Life Support (BLS), Advanced Life Support (ALS), and Non-emergency Ambulance Transportation.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid Transportation Services rules, when is prior authorization required for nonemergency ambulance service to eligible recipients?
answer: Prior authorization is required for all nonemergency ambulance service rendered to eligible Alabama Medicaid recipients 100 miles or more one way where medical care is received.

citations.quote: All nonemergency ambulance service rendered to eligible Alabama Medicaid recipients 100 miles or more one way where medical care is received, requires prior authorization.

question: According to Rule No. 560-X-18-.04 Scope of Ambulance Transportation Service Operations, what must documentation state to show ambulance service necessity?
answer: Documentation must state the condition(s) that show necessity of ambulance service, and indicate why patient could not be transported by another mode of transportation.

citations.quote: Documentation must state the condition(s) that show necessity of ambulance service, (and indicate why patient could not be transported by another mode of transportation).

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-18-.07 Time Limitation for Filing Medicaid Claims, within what timeframe must a provider submit claims for payment to the fiscal agent for Medicaid?
answer: Claims for payment shall be submitted to the fiscal agent for Medicaid within one year of the date of service.

citations.quote: Claims for payment (appropriate forms provided by fiscal agent for Medicaid) from provider of service shall be submitted to fiscal agent for Medicaid within one year of the date of service.

question: Where must all written or verbal communications pertaining to Alabama Medicaid recipients from out-of-state physicians or providers of ambulance transportation be referred?
answer: Alabama Medicaid Agency, 501 Dexter Avenue, Montgomery, Alabama 36104.

citations.quote: All written or verbal communications pertaining to Alabama Medicaid recipients, from out-of-state physicians or providers of ambulance transportation, will be referred to Alabama Medicaid Agency, 501 Dexter Avenue, Montgomery, Alabama 36104.

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-18-.13 Providers of Ambulance Service Responsibilities, what criminal penalty applies to a person who with intent to defraud or deceive knowingly makes a false statement or representation of material fact in a Medicaid claim or application?
answer: The person shall be guilty of a felony.

citations.quote: (1) Act No. 645 passed by the 1976 Regular Session of the Legislature of Alabama provided that any person who, with intent to defraud or deceive, makes or causes to be made, any false statement or representation of material fact in any claim or application for any payment, regardless of the amount from Alabama Medicaid Agency, knowing the same to be false, shall be guilty of a felony.

question: What must the Alabama Medicaid Agency ensure for eligible recipients with no other means of transportation under the Non-Emergency Transportation Program?
answer: The Alabama Medicaid Agency must ensure that transportation for Medicaid covered medical services is available for all eligible recipients in the state who have no other means of transportation.

citations.quote: As the State Agency for administering the Non-Emergency Transportation Program, under Title XIX of the Social Security Act, the Alabama Medicaid Agency must ensure that transportation for Medicaid covered medical services is available for all eligible recipients in the state who have no other means of transportation.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid Non-Emergency Transportation rules, by when must a reimbursement request for Non-Emergency Transportation resulting from urgent care be made?
answer: The request for reimbursement must be made the first business day after the transportation need has occurred.

citations.quote: (b) Request for reimbursements for Non-Emergency Transportation as a result of urgent care, must be made the first business day after the transportation need has occurred.

question: According to Rule 560-X-18-.20 NET Escorts, what documentation must Alabama Medicaid obtain before reimbursing escort services for a recipient age 21 or over?
answer: The Alabama Medicaid Agency must obtain a medical certification statement from the individual requesting an escort before reimbursement can be made, documenting the recipient is physically or mentally challenged such as blind, deaf, intellectually disabled, mentally ill, or physically handicapped to such a degree that personal assistance is necessary.

citations.quote: The Alabama Medicaid Agency must obtain a medical certification statement from the individual requesting an escort for recipients age 21 and over before reimbursement can be made.

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-18-.22 Modes of NET, when are escorts allowed for wheelchair vans services?
answer: Escorts are allowed for wheelchair vans when prior approved by the Alabama Medicaid Agency.

citations.quote: Escorts are allowed for wheelchair vans when prior approved by the Alabama Medicaid Agency

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-18-.24, is transportation provided after the death of a Medicaid recipient a covered Non-Emergency Transportation service?
answer: No. Transportation provided after the death of a Medicaid recipient is listed as a non-covered NET service.

citations.quote: Rule No. 560-X-18-.24. Non-covered NET Services. (1) When appropriate free transportation is available. (2) any travel when the Medicaid recipient is not an occupant of the vehicle unless that would be the most economical transportation available; (3) meals and lodging for volunteer drivers; (4) the use of supplies such as oxygen, intravenous fluids, etc.; (5) transportation for any services other than those covered by Medicaid; (6) transportation provided after the death of a Medicaid recipient; (7) minibus or wheelchair van travel outside a 30-mile radius of the state boundary; (8) services for which prior approval is required but not obtained; and (9) services are not medically necessary or which are not provided in compliance with the provision of this chapter.

question: What licensing requirement applies to individual drivers under Alabama Medicaid Transportation Services rule 18?
answer: Individual driver(s) must possess a valid driver’s license.

citations.quote: (2) Individual driver(s) must possess a valid driver’s license.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid Rule 560-X-19-.01, what must occur before a hearing aid will be approved for a Medicaid eligible recipient?
answer: A medical examination and recommendation for a hearing evaluation by a licensed physician within sixty (60) days of the time of hearing aid fitting. This is mandatory.

citations.quote: (a) A hearing aid will not be approved for any Medicaid eligible recipient prior to a medical examination and recommendation for a hearing evaluation by a licensed physician, within sixty (60) days of the time of hearing aid fitting. This is mandatory.

question: What six items must a licensed audiologist submit in a written enrollment request to Medicaid's Fiscal Agent under Rule 560-X-19-.02?
answer: Name, Address, Specialty provider type, Social Security Number, Tax ID Number, and a copy of current State license.

citations.quote: Licensed audiologists desiring to participate in the Alabama Medicaid Program should furnish the following information in a written enrollment request to Medicaid's Fiscal Agent. (a) Name (b) Address (c) Specialty provider type (d) Social Security Number (e) Tax ID Number (f) Copy of current State license

question: Under Alabama Medicaid Chapter 19 Hearing Services rule (4), when may a provider bill an Alabama Medicaid recipient directly?
answer: Providers may bill an Alabama Medicaid recipient only when the recipient has exhausted all of his/her allowed Medicaid benefits or when the service rendered is a non-covered service.

citations.quote: Providers may bill an Alabama Medicaid recipient only when the recipient has exhausted all of his/her allowed Medicaid benefits or when the service rendered is a non-covered service.

question: On which page of Chapter One General does Rule 560-X-1-.07 Provider Rights and Responsibilities appear according to the Table of Contents?
answer: Page 3

citations.quote: 560-X-1-.07 Provider Rights and Responsibilities 3

question: According to the table of contents on page 2, on what page is Rule 560-X-1-.25 Copayment (Cost-Sharing) listed?

citations.quote: 560-X-1-.25 Copayment (Cost-Sharing) 20

question: Which agency certifies aged, blind, and disabled applicants for the Federal Supplemental Security Income Program under Rule No. 560-X-1-.04?
answer: The Social Security Administration certifies aged, blind, and disabled applicants for the Federal Supplemental Security Income Program.

citations.quote: (1) The Social Security Administration certifies aged, blind, and disabled applicants for the Federal Supplemental Security Income (SSI) Program.

question: According to Rule No. 560-X-1-.06 Fiscal Agent, where should providers direct unresolved claims problems or dissatisfaction with the fiscal agent's response?
answer: Providers should direct unresolved problems or dissatisfaction with the fiscal agent's response to the Alabama Medicaid Agency at 501 Dexter Avenue, Montgomery, Alabama 36104, telephone (334) 242-5010.

citations.quote: Only unresolved problems or provider dissatisfaction with the response of the fiscal agent should be directed to Alabama Medicaid Agency, 501 Dexter Avenue, Montgomery, Alabama 36104, telephone number, (334) 242-5010.

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-1-.08 Recipient Rights and Responsibilities, what right does a recipient have if they believe their free choice of provider has been denied or impaired?
answer: The recipient has the right to request a fair hearing before the Alabama Medicaid Agency.

citations.quote: A recipient who believes that his/her free choice of provider has been denied or impaired has the right to request a fair hearing before the Alabama Medicaid Agency.

question: How many digits does an Alabama Medicaid recipient identification number contain and what are the possible first three digits?
answer: The identification number contains 13 digits and the first three digits will be "500" or "530".

citations.quote: The identification number of Medicaid eligible recipients contains 13 digits. The first three will be "500" or “530”.

question: Under Rule 560-X-1-.11, which individuals are excepted from receiving a plastic Medicaid card and receive a paper card instead?
answer: Certain unborns; recipients certified with a pseudo number; Medicare Savings Programs other than QMB; and recipients certified for a closed period of retroactive eligibility will receive a paper Medicaid card. Medicaid recipients residing in a long term care facility will not receive a plastic Medicaid card.

citations.quote: Individuals certified eligible for Medicaid will receive a plastic Medicaid Card through the mail with the following exceptions: certain unborns; recipients certified with a pseudo number; Medicare Savings Programs other than QMB; and recipients certified for a closed period of retroactive eligibility. These individuals will receive a paper Medicaid card. Also, Medicaid recipients residing in a long term care facility will not receive a plastic Medicaid card.

question: According to the Alabama Medicaid Administrative Code excerpt, must sites providing laboratory testing services to Medicaid recipients be CLIA certified?
answer: Yes. All sites providing laboratory testing services to Medicaid recipients, either directly by provider, or through contract, must be Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) certified to provide the level of testing complexity required.

citations.quote: All sites providing laboratory testing services to Medicaid recipients, either directly by provider, or through contract, must be Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) certified to provide the level of testing complexity required.

question: For QMB recipients, what Part A inpatient hospital cost-sharing does Medicaid cover for any inpatient admission?
answer: Medicaid covers the inpatient hospital deductible less any applicable copay, coinsurance days and lifetime reserve days for any inpatient admission.

citations.quote: For QMB recipients, the inpatient hospital deductible less any applicable copay, coinsurance days and lifetime reserve days are covered services for any inpatient admission.

question: When a provider's claim for service is rejected by the Medicare carrier as 'Medicare non-covered service' but is a covered Medicaid service, what should be sent to the Medicaid fiscal agent for payment?
answer: A Medicaid claim form, completed in accordance with instructions in the Alabama Medicaid Provider Manual, with a copy of the Medicare rejection statement, should be sent to the Medicaid fiscal agent for payment.

citations.quote: If the provider's claim for service is rejected by the Medicare carrier as "Medicare non-covered service" but is a covered Medicaid service, a Medicaid claim form, completed in accordance with instructions in the Alabama Medicaid Provider Manual, with a copy of the Medicare rejection statement, should be sent to the Medicaid fiscal agent for payment.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid Rule No. 560-X-1-.17, what is the time limit for a clean claim to be received by the fiscal agent to be considered timely?
answer: A timely claim is a clean claim which is received by the fiscal agent within one year of the date of service, unless a different limitation is specifically provided elsewhere in this Code.

citations.quote: A timely claim is a clean claim which is received by the fiscal agent within one year of the date of service, unless a different limitation is specifically provided elsewhere in this Code.

question: According to Rule No. 560-X-1-.18 Provider and Recipient Signature Requirements, what must a Designee indicate next to his/her signature?
answer: The Designee must indicate his/her relationship to the recipient next to his/her signature, e.g., spouse, power of attorney, authorized representative, etc.

citations.quote: The Designee must indicate his/her relationship to the recipient next to his/her signature (e.g. spouse, power of attorney, authorized representative, etc.).

question: Under what limited circumstances does Alabama Medicaid accept stamped signatures?
answer: Stamped signatures are not accepted except for claim forms as described in subsection (2)(b)(1) below, and in accordance with the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 for an author with a physical disability who can provide proof to Medicaid of inability to sign due to disability.

citations.quote: (d) Stamped signatures are not accepted except in the following limited circumstances: 1) Claim forms as described in subsection (2)(b)(1) below; 2) In accordance with the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 in the case of an author with a physical disability who can provide proof to Medicaid of his or her inability to sign his or her signature due to disability.

question: For hard copy Medicaid referral forms, are photocopied physician signatures acceptable?
answer: No. An original signature of the physician or duly authorized representative is required; photocopied signatures will not be accepted.

citations.quote: For hard copy referrals, the printed, typed, or stamped name of the primary care physician with an original signature of the physician or duly authorized representative is required. Photocopied signatures will not be accepted.

question: How may an illiterate recipient sign a Medicaid claim form?
answer: An illiterate recipient may make their mark, for example 'X', witnessed by someone with their dated signature and printed name after the phrase 'witnessed by.'

citations.quote: Illiterate recipients may make their mark, for example, "X" witnessed by someone with their dated signature and printed name after the phrase "witnessed by."

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-1-.21 Provider Medicaid Records Inspection/Audit, how long must Alabama Medicaid providers retain detailed records?
answer: Providers must retain records for a period of three years plus the current year.

citations.quote: These records will be retained for a period of three years plus the current year.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid Rule No. 560-X-1-.22, what must a Provider ALERT include when the Agency supersedes a promulgated rule during a state of emergency proclamation?
answer: The Provider ALERT must state the affected rule and have an explanation as to why it is superseding the rule, and it must specifically relate the reason to the emergency proclamation.

citations.quote: The Provider ALERT must state the affected rule and have an explanation as to why it is superseding the rule. It must specifically relate the reason to the emergency proclamation

question: Under Rule No. 560-X-1-.24 Limitations on Providers, when may the Alabama Medicaid Agency terminate an existing provider contract?
answer: The Agency may terminate an existing contract when it determines that during the last fiscal year the provider has provided services to Medicaid-only recipients not exceeding five claims and/or $100.00, or the provider has not submitted any claims in the previous 18 months.

citations.quote: The Alabama Medicaid Agency may terminate an existing contract of a provider when the Agency determines that during the last fiscal year the provider has provided services to Medicaid-only recipients not exceeding five claims and/or $100.00 or the provider has not submitted any claims in the previous 18 months.

question: According to Rule No. 560-X-1-.25 Copayment (Cost-Sharing), for which services are Medicaid recipients required to pay the designated copayment amount?
answer: Medicaid recipients are required to pay the designated copayment amount for physician office visits (including optometric), inpatient hospital admissions, outpatient hospital visits, rural health clinic visits, durable medical equipment, medical supplies, and pharmaceutical services, including Medicare crossovers.

citations.quote: Rule No. 560-X-1-.25 Copayment (Cost-Sharing). (1) Medicaid recipients are required to pay the designated copayment amount for the following services (including Medicare crossovers): (a) Physician office visits (including optometric) (b) Inpatient hospital admissions (c) Outpatient hospital visits (d) Rural health clinic visits (e) Durable Medical Equipment (f) Medical Supplies (g) Pharmaceutical

question: Who must refer transplant candidates under Alabama Medicaid Rule No. 560-X-1-.27 Organ Transplants?
answer: All transplant candidates must be from referrals by EPSDT or the primary physician.

citations.quote: (2) All transplant candidates must be from referrals by EPSDT or the primary physician.

question: May Alabama Medicaid recipients be billed for the difference between the submitted amount and the global payment for transplant services?
answer: No. The global payment represents full payment for all services associated with the transplant and recipients may not be billed for the difference between the submitted amount and the global payment.

citations.quote: The global payment represents full payment for all services associated with the transplant. Recipients may not be billed for the difference between the submitted amount and the global payment.

question: According to the Alabama Medicaid Administrative Code excerpt, what is done with charges to Medicaid that exceed actual invoice costs for eligible 340B entities?
