question: How many days of hospital bed reservation may not be charged to a Medicaid resident temporarily absent due to hospital admission?
answer: The first four days are covered without charge; neither Medicaid residents, nor their families, nor their personal representative may be charged for reservation of a bed for the first four days of any period during which a Medicaid resident is temporarily absent due to admission to a hospital.

citations.quote: Neither Medicaid residents, nor their families, nor their personal representative, may be charged for reservation of a bed for the first four days of any period during which a Medicaid resident is temporarily absent due to admission to a hospital.

question: What is the maximum length of a therapeutically indicated visit for a nursing facility resident to home, relatives, or friends?
answer: The visit does not exceed three days per visit, or six days per quarter, and visits may not be combined to exceed the three-day limit.

citations.quote: Nursing Facility the visit does not exceed three days per visit or six days per quarter. Visits may not be combined to exceed the three-day limit.

question: How long may a nursing facility use an individual as a nurse aide without the individual having completed an approved training and competency evaluation program?
answer: No more than four months.

citations.quote: A nursing facility must not use (on a full-time, temporary, per diem, or other basis) any individual as a nurse aide in the facility for more than four months unless the individual has completed training and a competency evaluation program approved by the state.

question: If a nursing facility admits a resident with MI/ID without first obtaining the required Level I Screening, Level I Determination and Level II Determination from the Department of Mental Health, what will Alabama Medicaid Agency do with Medicaid payments?
answer: The Alabama Medicaid Agency will recoup all Medicaid payments for nursing facility services from the date of the resident’s admission and continuing until the Level I Determination or Level II Determination, if applicable, is received.

citations.quote: If the nursing facility fails to obtain the Level I Screening, Level I Determination and Level II Determination, if applicable, made by the Department of Mental Health prior to admitting the resident into their facility, the Alabama Medicaid Agency will recoup all Medicaid payments for nursing facility services from the date of the resident’s admission and continuing until the Level I Determination or Level II Determination, if applicable is received.

question: According to the Nursing Facility criteria for Mobility ADL assistance, does the need for a wheelchair, walker, crutch, cane, or other mobility aid by itself meet the requirement?
answer: No. The individual requires physical assistance from another person for mobility on an ongoing basis, and the need for a wheelchair, walker, crutch, cane, or other mobility aid shall not by itself be considered to meet this requirement.

citations.quote: The need for a wheelchair, walker, crutch, cane, or other mobility aid shall not by itself be considered to meet this requirement.

question: Who must reimburse the nursing facility if a resident transferred from an inpatient psychiatric hospital for a two-week trial period leaves before the two weeks elapse?
answer: The inpatient psychiatric hospital is responsible for reimbursing the nursing facility.

citations.quote: If the resident leaves the nursing facility before the two-week period has elapsed, the inpatient psychiatric hospital is responsible for reimbursing the nursing facility.

question: According to the July 2026 Alabama Medicaid provider manual, what resident threshold causes a nursing facility to be classified as a mental disease facility?
answer: More than fifty percent (50%) of the residents receive care because of disability in functioning resulting from a mental disease.

citations.quote: More than fifty percent (50%) of the residents receive care because of disability in functioning resulting from a mental disease.

question: For nursing facilities classified as institutions for mental diseases for Medicaid payment purposes, what age limitations apply to Medicaid payments?
answer: Unless the facility is JCAHO-accredited as an inpatient psychiatric facility, payments are limited to Medicaid residents who are 65 years of age and older. If the facility is JCAHO-accredited as an inpatient psychiatric facility, payments may be made on behalf of individuals who are under age 21 or are 65 years of age and older.

citations.quote: In such facilities, unless the facility is JCAHO-accredited as an inpatient psychiatric facility, payments are limited to Medicaid residents who are 65 years of age and older.
If the facility is JCAHO-accredited as an inpatient psychiatric facility, payments may be made on behalf of the individuals who are under age 21 or are 65 years of age and older.

question: When must a nursing facility provider submit its complete uniform cost report for a fiscal year ending June 30?
answer: Medicaid must receive the complete uniform cost report on or before September 15, or the next working day if September 15 falls on a state holiday or weekend.

citations.quote: Medicaid must receive the complete uniform cost report on or before September 15. Should September 15 fall on a state holiday or weekend, the complete uniform cost report is due the next working day.

question: What must accompany the medical record when submitting LTC records for approval?
answer: The LTC Gainwell Cover Sheet from the web portal must accompany the medical record.

citations.quote: When submitting records the LTC Gainwell Cover Sheet from the web portal must accompany the medical record.

question: Which documents must a Medicaid certified ICF/IID facility maintain for new admissions to support ICF/IID level of care needs for Medicaid retrospective reviews?
answer: A fully completed Medicaid Patient Status Notification (Form 199); a fully completed ICF/IID Admission and Evaluation Data (Form XIX-LTC-18-22); the resident's physical history; the resident's psychological history; the resident's interim rehabilitation plan; and a social evaluation of the resident.

citations.quote: Nursing Facility 26 All Medicaid certified ICF/IID facilities are required to complete and maintain the following documents in their files for Medicaid retrospective reviews. These documents support the ICF/IID level of care needs. • New Admissions A fully completed Medicaid Patient Status Notification (Form 199). A fully completed ICF/IID Admission and Evaluation Data (Form XIX-LTC- 18-22). The resident's physical history. The resident's psychological history. The resident's interim rehabilitation plan. A social evaluation of the resident.

question: Does Alabama Medicaid require a copayment for services provided by nursing facility providers?
answer: No. Copayment does not apply to services provided by nursing facility providers.

citations.quote: 26.5 Cost Sharing (Copayment) Copayment does not apply to services provided by nursing facility providers.

question: For Alabama Medicaid nursing facility claims, which diagnosis code set applies based on date of service?
answer: ICD-9 codes should be used for claims submitted with dates of service prior to or equal to 09/30/2015. ICD-10 codes should be used for claims submitted with dates of service on/after 10/01/2015.

citations.quote: NOTE: ICD-9 codes should be used for claims submitted with dates of service prior to or equal to 09/30/2015. ICD-10 codes should be used for claims submitted with dates of service on/after 10/01/2015.

question: According to page 20 of the July 2026 Alabama Medicaid provider manual, who holds the copyright for the CPT and CDT code descriptors?
answer: The Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) and Current Dental Terminology (CDT) code descriptors are copyright © 2026 American Medical Association and © 2026 American Dental Association.

citations.quote: The Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) and Current Dental Terminology (CDT) codes descriptors, and other data are copyright © 2026 American Medical Association and © 2026 American Dental Association (or such other date publication of CPT and CDT). All rights reserved. Applicable FARS/DFARS apply.

question: What provider type is assigned to Pharmacy providers in Alabama Medicaid?
answer: Pharmacy providers are assigned provider type 24 (Pharmacy).

citations.quote: Pharmacy providers are assigned a provider type of 24 (Pharmacy).

question: What must providers of specialty drugs include in the letter requesting enrollment with the Alabama Medicaid Agency?
answer: Providers of specialty drugs shall list the names of the drugs for which they intend to request reimbursement as well as the GCN or NDC numbers for each drug in the letter requesting enrollment with the Alabama Medicaid Agency.

citations.quote: Providers of specialty drugs shall list the names of the drugs for which they intend to request reimbursement as well as the GCN or NDC numbers for each drug in the letter requesting enrollment with the Alabama Medicaid Agency.

question: What is the monthly outpatient pharmacy prescription limit for Alabama Medicaid recipients except those specified?
answer: The number of outpatient pharmacy prescriptions is limited to four brand name drugs / five total drugs per month per recipient, and in no case can total prescriptions exceed ten per month per recipient.

citations.quote: The number of outpatient pharmacy prescriptions for all recipients except as specified below is limited to four brand name drugs/ five total drugs per month per recipient. In no case can total prescriptions exceed ten per month per recipient.

question: What signature requirement applies to Schedule II drug prescriptions under Alabama Medicaid?
answer: Schedule II drug prescriptions require the manual signature of the prescribing physician before dispensing; stamped or typewritten signatures are not acceptable.

citations.quote: Schedule II drug prescriptions require the manual signature of the prescribing physician before dispensing. Stamped or typewritten signatures are not acceptable.

question: In an emergency where a pharmacy cannot contact the prescribing provider for a non-compliant written prescription, what must the pharmacy do if a compliant prescription cannot be obtained within 72 hours?
answer: The pharmacy must withdraw the claim.

citations.quote: If a compliant prescription cannot be obtained within 72 hours, the pharmacy must withdraw the claim.

question: For Alabama Medicaid pharmacy substitution code 8, what must a provider make available in the event of an audit?
answer: Documentation to validate product unavailability.

citations.quote: 8=Substitution Allowed-Generic Drug Not Available in Marketplace-This value is used when the prescriber has indicated, in a manner specified by prevailing law, that generic substitution is permitted and the brand product is dispensed since the generic is not currently manufactured, distributed, or is temporarily unavailable. (In the event of an audit, provider shall make available documentation to validate product unavailability).

question: Under Alabama Medicaid Pharmacy policy, what condition must be met for a prescription to be split billed between Medicaid and patient cash payment?
answer: A maximum unit override must be requested by the provider and denied. If the override is denied, the excess quantity above the maximum unit limit is non-covered and the recipient can be charged as cash for that amount.

citations.quote: In other words, for a prescription to be “split billed” (the maximum unit allowed paid by Medicaid and the remainder paid by the patient), a maximum unit override must be requested by the provider and denied.

If the override is denied, then the excess quantity above the maximum unit limit is non-covered and the recipient can be charged as a cash recipient for that amount in excess of the maximum unit limit.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid's three-month maintenance medication policy, what stability requirement must a recipient meet before the State will reimburse a provider for dispensing a three month supply?
answer: The recipient must demonstrate 60 consecutive days of stable therapy (same strength and dose) within a 90 day timeframe, according to Medicaid claims data, prior to the State reimbursing the provider for dispensing a three month supply.

citations.quote: The recipient must demonstrate 60 consecutive days of stable therapy (same strength and dose) within a 90 day timeframe, according to Medicaid claims data, prior to the State reimbursing the provider for dispensing a three month supply.

question: What is the maximum number of refills allowed for a non-controlled prescription under Alabama Medicaid, and what is the claim outcome if the limit is exceeded?
answer: Non-controlled prescriptions cannot exceed eleven refills. Medicaid will deny claims for prescription refills exceeding eleven for non-controlled prescriptions.

citations.quote: Prescriptions cannot exceed eleven refills for non-controlled prescriptions and five refills for Control III-V prescriptions. Medicaid will deny claims for prescription refills exceeding eleven for non-controlled prescriptions and five for Control III-V prescriptions.

question: What utilization percentage defines a timely refill for opioid agonist and opioid partial agonist claims under Alabama Medicaid?

citations.quote: Pharmacy Early/Timely Refills Medicaid allows timely refills, defined as utilization of 85% of opioid agonist and opioid partial agonist claims, 90% of drugs on the 3-month maintenance list, and 75% of all other medications.

question: What is the maximum payable amount per claim for a compounded product under Alabama Medicaid, and to whom should override requests exceeding that amount be referred?
answer: The maximum payable amount is $200 per claim. Requests for overrides for compounded products that exceed $200 should be referred to Acentra Health at 1 (800) 748-0130.

citations.quote: The maximum payable amount for a compounding product is $200 per claim.
Requests for overrides for compounded products that exceed $200 should be referred to Acentra Health at 1 (800) 748-0130.

question: How may long term care facilities bill OTC insulins covered by the Medicaid pharmacy program?
answer: By submitting for payment the NDC number utilized.

citations.quote: Long term care facilities may bill OTC insulins covered by the Medicaid pharmacy program by submitting for payment the NDC number utilized.

question: How should TPN prescriptions/orders be billed under Alabama Medicaid?
answer: TPN prescriptions/orders should be billed using a compound pharmacy claim based on a month’s supply.

citations.quote: TPN prescriptions/orders should be billed using a compound pharmacy claim based on a month’s supply.

question: According to the July 2026 Pharmacy manual, what must eligible 340B entities do after designation?
answer: They shall notify Medicaid of their designation as a 340B provider.

citations.quote: Eligible 340B entities are identified on the Department of Health and Human Service’s website. These entities shall notify Medicaid of their designation as a 340B provider.

question: What is the objective of the Drug Utilization Review (DUR) program according to Alabama Medicaid?
answer: To improve the quality of pharmaceutical care by ensuring that prescriptions are appropriate, medically necessary, and unlikely to result in adverse medical outcomes.

citations.quote: Pharmacy 27 27.2.7 Drug Utilization Review (DUR) The objective of DUR is to improve the quality of pharmaceutical care by ensuring that prescriptions are appropriate, medically necessary, and unlikely to result in adverse medical outcomes.

question: What three components must Prospective DUR include at the point of sale or distribution before each prescription is filled or delivered to a Medicaid recipient?
answer: Prospective DUR must include screening, patient counseling, and use of patient profiles.

citations.quote: Pharmacy Prospective DUR Prospective DUR (Pro-DUR) is required at the point of sale or distribution before each prescription is filled or delivered to a Medicaid recipient. It must include screening, patient counseling, and use of patient profiles.

question: What conflict code must a pharmacist enter in response to a therapeutic duplication alert?
answer: TD

citations.quote: The pharmacist should respond to alerts with the appropriate conflict code. For example, enter TD for Therapeutic Duplicate in response to a therapeutic duplication alert.

question: What does the manual state about using the letter O instead of zero in intervention codes?
answer: Intervention codes contain the number zero, not the letter O. Using the letter O will cause your claim to deny online.

citations.quote: NOTE: Intervention codes contain the number zero, not the letter O. Using the letter O will cause your claim to deny online.

question: What federal authorization number may be used for a 72-hour emergency supply of a covered outpatient prescription drug, and when is its use permitted?
answer: Authorization number 0000999527 may be used for a 72-hour emergency supply, and it is to be used only in cases of emergency.

citations.quote: Federal Law also makes a provision for a 72-hour supply by using the following authorization number: 0000999527. This number is to be used only in cases of emergency.

question: Within what timeframe must a provider notify patients after receiving notice of a recall for items already dispensed?
answer: Notification to patients must occur within 24 hours of the recall receipt.

citations.quote: (b) Any recalled items dispensed to patients shall be retrieved and quarantined; notification to patients must occur within 24 hours of the recall receipt.

question: May pharmacists or pharmacy staff change a Medicaid recipient’s therapy based on the cost of the medication?
answer: No. Pharmacists/pharmacy staff shall not change a Medicaid recipient’s therapy based on the cost of the medication without prior written approval from the prescriber and noted in the patient chart.

citations.quote: Pharmacists/pharmacy staff shall not change a Medicaid recipient’s therapy based on the cost of the medication without prior written approval from the prescriber and noted in the patient chart.

question: What value must a provider enter in the prior authorization type code field to indicate a copay exemption for a Native American Indian presenting an active user letter issued by Indian Health Services?

citations.quote: The provider must enter a value of ‘4’ in the prior authorization type code field indicating co-pay exemption for a Native American Indian with an active user letter.

question: Within how long must Alabama Medicaid pharmacy providers file claims?
answer: Medicaid requires all claims for Pharmacy providers to be filed within one year of the date of service.

citations.quote: Medicaid requires all claims for Pharmacy providers to be filed within one year of the date of service.

question: What is the Prescription Origin Code requirement for Alabama Medicaid pharmacy billing and what are its valid values?
answer: The Prescription Origin Code is required and indicates the means used to deliver a prescription to a pharmacy. Valid values are 0 = Not Known, 1 = Written, 2 = Telephone, 3 = Electronic, 4 = Facsimile, 5 = Pharmacy.

citations.quote: 27.5.7 Prescription Origin Code The code indicating the means used to deliver a prescription to a pharmacy – this is a required field. Valid values are: 0 = Not Known 1 = Written 2 = Telephone 3 = Electronic 4 = Facsimile 5 = Pharmacy

question: How long is a non-controlled prescription reimbursable by Medicaid, and can additional refills be authorized after 12 months have expired?
answer: Non-controlled prescriptions are reimbursable by Medicaid for up to 12 months from the date of the original dispensing date. No additional refills can be authorized after 12 months; a new prescription should be obtained after 12 months from the date of the original dispensing date.

citations.quote: Non-controlled prescriptions are reimbursable by Medicaid for up to 12 months from the date of the original dispensing date.

Can I receive authorization for additional refills from the prescribing physician after the 12 months have expired? No. A new prescription should be obtained after 12 months from the date of the original dispensing date.

question: Can a pharmacy provider advertise waived copays for their Medicaid patients?
answer: No. Advertising the waiver of or routinely waiving Medicaid copayments is a prohibited remuneration under Section 22-1-11, Code of Alabama and 1128B of the Social Security Act.

citations.quote: Can a pharmacy provider advertise waived copays for their Medicaid patients? No. Advertising the waiver of or routinely waiving Medicaid copayments is a prohibited remuneration under Section 22-1-11, Code of Alabama and 1128B of the Social Security Act (SSA).

question: What is the Alabama Board of Pharmacy exception to the requirement that dispensing location match the enrolled pharmacy’s NPI billing/service location?
answer: Dispensing from the permitted location must match the billing/service location of the enrolled pharmacy’s NPI. The only exception allowed is Section 34-23-70(e) of the Alabama Practice of Pharmacy Act, which exempts federally qualified health centers, except with respect to controlled substances, from the prohibition on pick-up stations/intermediaries, authorizing an eligible FQHC to fill certain prescriptions at one location and deliver medications to clinics for patient pick-up subject to board review.

citations.quote: Pharmacy 27 Board of Pharmacy for that particular location, and the dispensing from that permitted location must match the billing/service location of the enrolled pharmacy’s NPI. *The only exception allowed by Alabama Board of Pharmacy is: Section 34-23-70 of the Alabama Practice of Pharmacy Act 205: Management; display of permit and license; poisons; prescription requirements; violations: (e) No pharmacy shall authorize any person, firm, or business establishment to serve as a pick-up station or intermediary for the purpose of having prescriptions filled or delivered, whether for profit or gratuitously. Except with respect to controlled substances, any facility recognized as a federally qualified health center, as defined in 42 U.S.C. §1396d(l)(2)(B), operating health care practices and providing pharmacy services in the state is expressly exempt from this subsection. Each eligible federally qualified health center is authorized to fill certain prescriptions at one location and deliver medications to clinics for patient pick-up subject to the review of the board.

question: According to page 34 of the July 2026 manual, who holds the copyright for the CPT and CDT code descriptors referenced on that page?
answer: The Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) and Current Dental Terminology (CDT) codes descriptors, and other data are copyright © 2026 American Medical Association and © 2026 American Dental Association.

citations.quote: The Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) and Current Dental Terminology (CDT) codes descriptors, and other data are copyright © 2026 American Medical Association and © 2026 American Dental Association (or such other date publication of CPT and CDT). All rights reserved. Applicable FARS/DFARS apply.

question: What provider type is assigned to physicians under Alabama Medicaid and what NPI requirement applies when filing a claim?
answer: Physicians are assigned provider type 31 (Physician). A 10-digit NPI is required when filing a claim.

citations.quote: Physicians are assigned a provider type of 31 (Physician).
NOTE: The 10-digit NPI is required when filing a claim.

question: According to the July 2026 Physician Specialty list, what code is assigned to Ophthalmology?

citations.quote: Physician 28 Specialty (Physician - 31) Code Ophthalmology 330

question: Which providers are listed as not meeting criteria for BUMP rates under Physician B?
answer: Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC), Rural Health Clinic (RHC), Health Department (ADPH), Teaching Facility, OB/GYNs, and Nursing Facility.

citations.quote: The following providers do not meet criteria for BUMP rates: 1. Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) 2. Rural Health Clinic (RHC) 3. Health Department (ADPH) 4. Teaching Facility 5. OB/GYNs 6. Nursing Facility

question: Which provider types are eligible for Physician Retention and Access Improvement Program supplemental payments under the July 2026 manual?
answer: Physicians (as defined in state plan), Physician Assistants, Nurse Practitioners (NPs), Certified Nurse Wives (CNMs), Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetists (CRNAs) or Anesthesiology Assistants (AAs), Clinical Psychologists, and Optometrists.

citations.quote: 1. Be one of the following provider types: a. Physicians (as defined in state plan) b. Physician Assistants c. Nurse Practitioners (NPs) d. Certified Nurse Wives (CNMs) e. Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetists (CRNAs) or Anesthesiology Assistants (AAs) f. Clinical Psychologists g. Optometrists

question: Under Section 28.2 Benefits and Limitations, what is the annual office visit benefit limit for Alabama Medicaid?
answer: Annual office visit benefit limits are 14 office visits per calendar year.

citations.quote: Annual office visit benefit limits are 14 office visits per calendar year.

question: Under what conditions will Alabama Medicaid pay for services furnished in another state?
answer: Alabama Medicaid will pay for out-of-state services provided to an Alabama Medicaid recipient to the same extent as in-state services when any of four conditions is met: medical services are needed due to a medical emergency; the recipient’s health would be endangered if required to travel to his state of residence; the state determines on medical advice that needed services are more readily available in the other state; or it is general practice for recipients in a particular locality to use medical resources in another state.

citations.quote: Alabama Medicaid will pay for services furnished in another state to the same extent it would pay for services furnished within its boundaries as long as the service is provided to an Alabama Medicaid recipient and any of four following conditions is met: (a) Medical services are needed due to a medical emergency. (b) Medical services are needed, and the recipient’s health would be endangered if he were required to travel to his state of residence. (c) The state determines, on the basis of medical advice, that the needed medical services, or necessary supplementary services, are more readily available in the other state. (d) It is general practice for recipients in a particular locality to use medical resources in another state.

question: What encrypted email address should Form 382 and all supporting documentation be submitted to for an out-of-state service request?
answer: out-of-state-request@medicaid.alabama.gov

citations.quote: Submit Form 382 along with all supporting documentation via encrypted email to: out-of-state-request@medicaid.alabama.gov

question: Under Alabama Medicaid reciprocal billing arrangements, which HCPCS modifiers must a regular physician use to identify services furnished by a substitute physician?
answer: The regular physician shall identify the services as substitute physician services by entering HCPCS modifier Q5 for Service Furnished by a Substitute Physician under a Reciprocal Arrangement or HCPCS modifier Q6 for Service Furnished by a Locum Tenens Physician after the procedure code.

citations.quote: The regular physician shall identify the services as substitute physician services by entering HCPCS modifier Q5 (Service Furnished by a Substitute Physician under a Reciprocal Arrangement) or HCPCS modifier Q6 (Service Furnished by a Locum Tenens Physician) after the procedure code.

question: When must Alabama Medicaid prescribers check the Alabama PDMP before prescribing a Schedule II controlled substance, and what is required if they do not check it?
answer: Effective October 1, 2021, prescribers of Medicaid eligible recipients are required to check the Alabama PDMP prior to prescribing a Schedule II controlled substance; if the prescriber does not check the PDMP, the prescriber is required to document the reason in the medical record.

citations.quote: In accordance with Section 5042 of the SUPPORT Act, effective October 1, 2021, prescribers of Medicaid eligible recipients are required to check the Alabama PDMP (Prescription Drug Monitoring Program) prior to prescribing a Schedule II controlled substance.
If the prescriber does not check the PDMP, the prescriber is required to document the reason in the medical record.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid, how must covered services furnished by a PA or CRNP be billed?
answer: Covered services furnished by the PA or CRNP must be billed under the PA’s or CRNP’s name and NPI as the rendering provider.

citations.quote: Covered services furnished by the PA or CRNP must be billed under the PA’s or CRNP’s name and NPI as the rendering provider.

question: What prior authorization and age restriction applies to CPT code 69210 in the outpatient hospital setting according to Alabama Medicaid?
answer: CPT 69210 requires a prior authorization and is restricted to ages 0-20 in the outpatient hospital setting.

citations.quote: **NOTE: CPT 69210 requires a prior authorization and is restricted to ages 0-20 in the outpatient hospital setting.**

question: Under Alabama Medicaid, when do CT scans require prior authorization for coverage?
answer: Effective for dates of service March 2, 2009, and thereafter, CT scans require prior authorization for coverage.

citations.quote: CT scans are covered as medically necessary. Effective for dates of service March 2, 2009, and thereafter, CT scans require prior authorization for coverage.

question: What is Alabama Medicaid's annual benefit limit for physician visits for examinations?
answer: Physician visits for examinations are counted toward a limit of 14 physician visits per year per recipient, with certified emergencies excepted.

citations.quote: Physician visits for examinations are counted as part of each recipient’s benefit limit of 14 physician visits per year. Exception: Certified Emergencies.

question: Which ICD-10 diagnosis codes must be used on a claim form when billing normal newborn care under the mother’s Medicaid number?
answer: Z76.1-Z76.2 and Z00.129 must be used for ICD-10 for normal newborn care, and these diagnosis codes must be used on the claim form for consideration of payment.

citations.quote: When billing under the mother’s Medicaid number, use diagnosis codes Z76.1-Z76.2 and Z00.129 for ICD-10, for normal newborn care. These diagnosis codes must be used on the claim form for consideration of payment.

question: How are physician visits for second opinions counted toward a recipient's annual benefit limit under Alabama Medicaid?
answer: Physician visits for second opinions are counted as part of each recipient’s benefit limit of 14 physician visits per year.

citations.quote: Physician visits for second opinions are counted as part of each recipient’s benefit limit of 14 physician visits per year.

question: For Alabama Medicaid medical necessity of denervation, what minimum pain relief must be documented from each diagnostic facet joint injection?
answer: Each diagnostic facet joint injection must provide a consistent minimum of 80% pain relief.

citations.quote: Physician All the following requirements must be met for medical necessity to be determined for denervation: 1) The recipient has had up to two medically reasonable and necessary diagnostic facet joint injections with each one providing a consistent minimum of 80% pain relief.

question: How does Alabama Medicaid pay for multiple or bilateral surgical procedures performed during the same operative session?
answer: Medicaid pays 100% for the procedure with the highest allowed amount and 50% of the allowed amount for each subsequent procedure, with procedures ranked by Medicaid allowed amount from highest to lowest.

citations.quote: When multiple surgical procedures or bilateral procedures are performed during the same operative session, Medicaid pays for the procedure with the highest allowed amount at 100% and 50% of the allowed amount for each subsequent procedure.
Procedures are ranked by Medicaid allowed amount (highest to lowest).

question: Within what timeframe must a recipient elect breast reconstruction after a mastectomy under Alabama Medicaid?
answer: The recipient must elect reconstruction within two years of the mastectomy surgery date.

citations.quote: The recipient elects reconstruction within two years of the mastectomy surgery date

question: Under Alabama Medicaid, where is physical therapy covered and where is it not covered?
answer: Physical therapy is not covered when provided in a physician’s office. It is covered only when prescribed by a physician or non-physician practitioner and provided in a hospital setting.

citations.quote: Physical Therapy is not covered when provided in a physician’s office. Physical therapy is covered only when prescribed by a physician or non-physician practitioner and provided in a hospital setting.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid Physician Services Coverage and Conditions, what is the billing status of non-invasive ear or pulse oximetry procedure codes 94760-94762 effective January 1, 2009?
answer: Effective January 1, 2009, non-invasive ear or pulse oximetry services procedure codes 94760-94762 will no longer be considered separately billable/payable by Medicaid for physician and outpatient services. The codes are considered bundled services which are included in Evaluation and Management codes for both physician and outpatient services.

citations.quote: Effective January 1, 2009, Non-invasive ear or pulse oximetry services (procedure codes 94760-94762) will no longer be considered separately billable/payable by Medicaid for physician and outpatient services.
These procedure codes, per policy dated July 2006, are considered bundled services which are included in Evaluation and Management codes for both physician and outpatient services.

question: Under Physician 28.2.4 Limitations on Services, how many physician visits is an Alabama Medicaid recipient limited to per calendar year?
answer: No more than a total of 14 physician visits in offices, hospital outpatient settings, nursing facilities, rural health clinics or Federally Qualified Health Centers per calendar year.

citations.quote: Within each calendar year each recipient is limited to no more than a total of 14 physician visits in offices, hospital outpatient settings, nursing facilities, rural health clinics or Federally Qualified Health Centers.

question: Effective January 1, 2023, what is the annual physician office visit maximum for Alabama Medicaid recipients receiving cancer treatment, and what informational procedure code requirement must be met to qualify?
answer: The annual physician office visit maximum is increased to 32 visits per calendar year for recipients receiving cancer treatment. To qualify, the claim must include one of the informational procedure codes 3300F, 3301F, S0353 or S0354 to identify the treatment stage, and a cancer diagnosis within the current calendar year must be in the recipient’s claims history.

citations.quote: Effective January 1, 2023, Alabama Medicaid will increase the annual physician office visit maximum to 32 for Medicaid recipients receiving cancer treatment during the calendar year (January -- December).

To qualify for this increase in annual physician office visits: 1. The claim must include one of the following informational procedure codes to identify the treatment stage: • 3300F: American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) state documented and reviewed (ONC) • 3301F: Cancer stage documented in medical record as metastatic and reviewed (ONC) • S0353: Treatment planning and care coordination management for cancer initial treatment • S0354: Treatment planning and care coordination management for cancer established patient with a change in regimen (Failure to provide one of the required informational procedure codes will cause the recipient to not be eligible for the 32 visits.)

question: Which CPT codes must accompany G2212 for office or other outpatient E&M services under Alabama Medicaid?
answer: G2212 must be filed with 99205 or 99215 for office or other outpatient E&M services.

citations.quote: • G2212 must be filed with 99205 or 99215 for office or other outpatient E&M services.

question: When the same physician bills both a hospital visit and a hospital discharge on the same day, which service is paid under Alabama Medicaid?
answer: Only the hospital discharge shall be paid; the hospital visit shall not be paid to the same physician on the same day.

citations.quote: A physician hospital visit and hospital discharge shall not be paid to the same physician on the same day. If both are billed, only the discharge shall be paid.

question: Under what condition may CPT codes 99291, 99292, 99466 and 99467 be billed with place of service 41, Ambulance?
answer: They may be billed by the physician providing the care of the critically ill or injured patient in place of service 41, Ambulance, if care is personally rendered by the physician providing the care of the critically ill or injured patient.

citations.quote: Procedure codes 99291, 99292, 99466 and 99467 may be billed by the physician providing the care of the critically ill or injured patient in place of service 41, Ambulance, if care is personally rendered by the physician providing the care of the critically ill or injured patient.

question: Can Subsequent Hospital Care codes 99231-99233 be billed on the same date of service as neonatal critical care codes 99468-99476?
answer: No. Subsequent Hospital Care codes 99231-99233 cannot be billed on the same date of service as neonatal critical care codes 99468-99476.

citations.quote: Subsequent Hospital Care codes (99231-99233) cannot be billed on the same date of service as neonatal critical care codes (99468-99476)

question: When a patient is transferred from the NICU to the pediatric unit, can critical care codes be used and what should be billed instead?
answer: Critical care codes cannot be used for transfers to the pediatric unit from the NICU; subsequent hospital care should be billed in these instances.

citations.quote: Transfers to the pediatric unit from the NICU cannot be billed using critical care codes. Subsequent hospital care would be billed in these instances.

question: Which individual procedures related to critical care may be billed in addition to procedure codes 99478-99480?
answer: Chest tube placement, Pericardiocentesis or thoracentesis, and Intracranial taps may be billed in addition to procedure codes 99478-99480.

citations.quote: Restrictions: No individual procedures related to critical care may be billed in addition to procedure codes 99478-99480 except: • Chest tube placement • Pericardiocentesis or thoracentesis • Intracranial taps

question: How should physicians bill CPT codes for outpatient dialysis services that are interrupted during a full month by hospitalization?
answer: The CPT codes described by age for physicians rendering outpatient dialysis services that are interrupted during a full month should be billed on a per day basis for the days of the month in which the outpatient ESRD related services were performed.

citations.quote: The CPT codes described by age for physicians rendering outpatient dialysis services that are interrupted during a full month should be billed on a per day basis.
These codes should be billed for the days of the month in which the outpatient ESRD related services were performed.

question: According to the July 2026 Alabama Medicaid provider manual, what medical record documentation is required to support coverage of hyperalimentation/TPN?
answer: Medical record documentation must include supporting evidence that the patient cannot be maintained on oral or enteral feedings and that due to severe pathology of the alimentary tract, hyperalimentation must be given in order to meet 100% of the patient’s nutritional needs. Physical signs, symptoms and test results indicating severe pathology of the alimentary tract must be clearly documented, including BUN, serum albumin, and phosphorus. Medical records must document inability to maintain weight during a trial of at least four weeks of enteral feeding.

citations.quote: • Medical record documentation must include supporting evidence that the patient cannot be maintained on oral or enteral feedings and that due to severe pathology of the alimentary tract, hyperalimentation must be given in order to meet 100% of the patient’s nutritional needs.

• Physical signs, symptoms and test results indicating severe pathology of the alimentary tract must be clearly documented in the medical record. This would include BUN, serum albumin, and phosphorus.
Medical records must document inability to maintain weight during a trial of at least four weeks of enteral feeding.

question: What minimum duration of enteral feeding trial must be documented as unsuccessful before IDPN or IPN can be billed under Alabama Medicaid?
answer: Medical records must document inability to maintain weight during a trial of at least four weeks of enteral feeding.

citations.quote: Medical records must document inability to maintain weight during a trial of at least four weeks of enteral feeding.

question: What is the Medicaid reimbursement rate for the administration fee for vaccines provided free of charge through the VFC Program?
answer: The rate is $8.00, and it is not the rate on the pricing file.

citations.quote: Physician 28 Medicaid reimburses administration fees for vaccines provided free of charge through the VFC Program. The rate for the administration fee is $8.00; it is not the rate on the pricing file.

question: Which modifier should Alabama Medicaid providers use to denote a repeat clinical laboratory test performed on the same date of service for the same recipient, and which modifier should be avoided for repeat lab procedures?
answer: Providers should use modifier 91 instead of modifier 76 for repeat lab procedures.

citations.quote: Repeat Lab Procedures Modifier 91 may be utilized to denote a repeat clinical laboratory test performed on the same date of service for the same recipient. Providers should use modifier 91 instead of modifier 76 for repeat lab procedures.

question: What is the timely filing limit for physician claims to Alabama Medicaid?
answer: Medicaid requires all claims for physicians to be filed within one year of the date of service.

citations.quote: Medicaid requires all claims for physicians to be filed within one year of the date of service.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid, when should a physician append Modifier 24 to an E&M service?
answer: Modifier 24 is used to indicate an evaluation and management service performed during a postoperative period for reason(s) unrelated to the original procedure. It is appropriate when a physician provides a surgical service related to one problem and, during the postoperative period or follow-up care for the surgery, provides an E&M service unrelated to the problem requiring the surgery.

citations.quote: Modifier 24 (Unrelated Evaluation and Management Service by the Same Physician During a Postoperative Period) The Physician may need to indicate that an evaluation and management service was performed during a postoperative period for a reason(s) unrelated to the original procedure.

From a coding perspective, modifier 24 is appropriate when a physician provides a surgical service related to one problem and, during the postoperative period or follow-up care for the surgery, provides and E&M service unrelated to the problem requiring the surgery.

question: When must a provider submit medical records with a hysterectomy consent form for Alabama Medicaid?
answer: Medical records are required only if the hysterectomy was performed due to unusual circumstances e.g., already sterile, life-threatening situation, or performed under a period or retroactive Medicaid eligibility. For a medically necessary hysterectomy performed for treatment of disease, the signed consent form alone is sufficient and no medical records need be submitted.

citations.quote: There is no need to submit medical records for hysterectomies that are medically necessary. However, if the hysterectomy was performed due to unusual circumstances (e.g., already sterile, life-threatening situation, or performed under a period or retroactive Medicaid eligibility), the provider must submit medical records and consent form by uploading or faxing the documents to the Web Portal.

If the hysterectomy was medically necessary, no additional medical records are needed. However, if the hysterectomy was performed due to unusual circumstances, the provider must upload the consent form and medical records via the Forms menu of the Alabama Medicaid Interactive Web Portal.

question: What procedure code should Rural Health Clinics/Independent Providers use for routine venipuncture collection under Alabama Medicaid?

citations.quote: Rural Health Clinics/Independent Providers should use procedure code 36415-90 for routine venipuncture collection, 36416-90 for collection for capillary blood specimen (eg, finger, heel, ear stick) and Q0091-90 for collection of Pap smear specimen.

question: What place of service codes are listed under section 36.5.4 for filing claims for independent rural health clinics?
answer: POS 11 Office; 21 Inpatient Hospital; 22 Outpatient Hospital; 23 Emergency Room – Hospital; 31 Skilled Nursing Facility or Nursing Facility; 32 Nursing Facility.

citations.quote: 36.5.4 Place of Service Codes The following place of service codes apply when filing claims for independent rural health clinics: POS Code Description 11 Office 21 Inpatient Hospital 22 Outpatient Hospital 23 Emergency Room – Hospital 31 Skilled Nursing Facility or Nursing Facility 32 Nursing Facility

question: What does page 12 of the July 2026 Rural Health Clinics/Independent section 36 indicate about its content?
answer: This page intentionally left blank.

citations.quote: Rural Health Clinics/Independent This page intentionally left blank.

question: When is administration of anesthesia a covered service under Alabama Medicaid?
answer: When administered by or directed by a duly licensed physician for a medical procedure that is covered by Medicaid.

citations.quote: Administration of anesthesia is a covered service when administered by or directed by a duly licensed physician for a medical procedure that is covered by Medicaid.

question: What conditions must be met for an anesthesiologist to perform a necessary task or medical procedure while concurrently medically directing CRNAs or AAs?
answer: The task or procedure may be executed only if it is immediately interruptible without compromising the wellbeing, quality of care, or health of the recipient and is executed in an area close enough to the operating rooms where the CRNAs and AAs are being medically directed to permit the physician to remain immediately physically available, e.g., the Post-Anesthesia Care Unit or receiving room.

citations.quote: A necessary task or medical procedure may be executed while concurrently medically directing CRNAs or AAs only if the task or procedure is one which may be: (1) immediately interruptible without compromising the wellbeing, quality of care, or health of the recipient and (2) is executed in an area close enough to the operating rooms where the CRNAs and AAs are being medically directed and that will permit the physician to remain in compliance with the requirements of being immediately physically available.
Examples of an “area close enough to the operating rooms” are the Post-Anesthesia Care Unit (PACU) or receiving room.

question: How much pre-induction preparation time and post-operative time may be included in Alabama Medicaid anesthesia billing?
answer: Up to 15 minutes are allowed for preparation of anesthesia before induction, and up to 15 minutes are allowed after the operation for transfer of the recipient to the receiving room, recovery room, or PACU.

citations.quote: Up to 15 minutes are allowed for the preparation of anesthesia, and up to 15 minutes are allowed after the operation (for transfer of the recipient to the receiving room, recovery room, or PACU).

question: What is the billing rate for regional anesthesia administered by the attending physician during a procedure under Alabama Medicaid?
answer: The physician's fee for administration of the anesthesia is billed at one-half the established rate for a comparable service when performed by an anesthesiologist.

citations.quote: When regional anesthesia (i.e., nerve block) is administered by the attending physician during a procedure, the physician's fee for administration of the anesthesia is billed at one-half the established rate for a comparable service when performed by an anesthesiologist.

question: Is standby anesthesia payable under Alabama Medicaid?
answer: No. Standby anesthesia is not payable under Medicaid.

citations.quote: Standby anesthesia is not payable under Medicaid.

question: Under Alabama Medicaid, what is the reimbursement limit and procedure code for an anesthesiologist’s management of a PCA pump administered through an IV line for post-operative pain?
answer: An anesthesiologist managing a PCA pump through an IV line is allowed a total of four units as a global payment regardless of how many days the recipient remains on the pump. Use procedure code 96522 for daily hospital management of intravenous patient-controlled analgesia.

citations.quote: When an anesthesiologist provides the management of the PCA pump through an IV line, the anesthesiologist will be allowed a total of four units and will be considered a global payment for the management regardless of the number of days the recipient remains on the pump.
Use procedure code 96522 for daily hospital management of intravenous patient-controlled analgesia.

question: What type of service should be used for billing anesthesia codes 00100-01997?
answer: Type of service “7” should be used for billing anesthesia codes (00100-01997).

citations.quote: Type of service “7” should be used for billing anesthesia codes (00100- 01997).

question: Which modifier must an anesthesiologist use when billing medically directed anesthesia services for one qualified individual, i.e., CRNA, AA, intern, resident or combinations of these individuals?
answer: QY

citations.quote: QY for medically directed services of 1 qualified individual, i.e., CRNA, AA, intern, resident or combinations of these individuals (effective for 01/01/99)

question: When an anesthesia provider bills for a recipient treated by a dental provider who is not assigned a Medicare NPI, what NPI should be reported on a paper CMS-1500 claim and in which block?
answer: Use OTH000 as the referring/attending NPI number in block 17a of the CMS-1500 claim form. For electronic 837P filing, use OTH000 in REF02 with ID qualifier 1G in REF01. Claims not containing this information will deny.

citations.quote: Anesthesiologists should use “OTH000” as the referring or attending NPI number for providers who are not assigned a NPI number by Medicare. For example, when providing anesthesia services for recipients who are being treated by dental providers, please use “OTH000” as the NPI number in block 17a of the CMS 1500 form. Use “OTH000” in REF02 and the ID qualifier 1G in REF 01 when filing claims electronically on the 837P.
If you file hard copy, the NPI number should be populated in block 17a of the CMS 1500 claim form.

question: According to Anesthesiology section 38.6 For More Information, in which chapter are CMS-1500 Claim Filing Instructions listed?
answer: Chapter 5

citations.quote: CMS-1500 Claim Filing Instructions Chapter 5

question: Is Medicaid reimbursement provided for the day of discharge for inpatient psychiatric services?
answer: No. Medicaid reimbursement is available for the day of admission, but not the day of discharge.

citations.quote: Medicaid reimbursement is available for the day of admission, but not the day of discharge.

question: How often must the Certificate of Needs form for recertification of need for continued inpatient psychiatric services be completed for recipients ages 21-64 after initial certification?
answer: At least every 30 days after initial certification.

citations.quote: The Certificate of Needs form or equivalent must be completed at least every 30 days after initial certification.

question: How frequently must the attending or staff physician review the plan of care for a psychiatric inpatient recipient ages 21-64?
answer: As needed or every 30 days.

citations.quote: The attending or staff physician and other appropriate staff involved in the care of the recipient must review the plan of care as needed or every 30 days.

question: To which encrypted email address must OPPCs related to the administering of medication(s) and MAR documentation be reported to Medicaid?
answer: adverseevents@medicaid.alabama.gov

citations.quote: The following OPPCs related to the administering of medication(s) and documentation provided in the medication administration records (MARs) must be reported to Medicaid by encrypted emailing of the required information to: adverseevents@medicaid.alabama.gov

question: Who is responsible for performing continued stay reviews on recipients who require continued inpatient hospitalization in psychiatric inpatient facilities for recipients ages 21-64?
answer: The hospital's utilization review personnel are responsible for performing continued stay reviews on recipients who require continued inpatient hospitalization.

citations.quote: 39.4 Continued Stay Reviews (CSR) The hospital's utilization review personnel are responsible for performing continued stay reviews on recipients who require continued inpatient hospitalization.

question: Where in the Alabama Medicaid manual can providers find UB-04 Claim Filing Instructions for Psychiatric Inpatient Hospitalization Treatment Facilities (Recipients ages 21-64) per section 39.6 For More Information?
answer: Chapter 5

citations.quote: Psychiatric Inpatient Hospitalization Treatment Facilities (Recipients ages 21-64) 39.6 For More Information This section contains a cross-reference to other relevant sections in the manual. Resource Where to Find It UB-04 Claim Filing Instructions Chapter 5

question: What phone number should providers call for questions about the ACHN program?

citations.quote: If you have any questions about this program, please contact the Provider Assistance Center at 1 (800) 688-7989.

question: What is the enrollment effective date for an ACHN PCP Group Agreement received by Gainwell on or before the 15th of a month with no errors?
answer: The first day of the following month.

citations.quote: The enrollment effective date for the ACHN PCP Group Agreement will the first day of the following month, if the agreement is received and contains no errors prior to the 15th of the month.

question: What must providers complete and submit in addition to the Medicaid PCP Group Agreement to qualify for ACHN participation rates and bonus payments?
answer: An ACHN PCP Network Participation Agreement to an ACHN, signed by the provider.

citations.quote: ACHN PCP Network Participation Agreement: In addition to the Medicaid PCP Group Agreement, providers must complete and submit an ACHN PCP Network Participation Agreement to an ACHN to qualify for participation rates and bonus payments.

question: What application must a provider complete to be added to an existing ACHN PCP Group Enrollment?
answer: An “Individual within a Group” application.

citations.quote: For providers who wish to be added to an existing ACHN PCP Group Enrollment, the provider must complete an “Individual within a Group” application.

question: What must a PCP Group do to continue receiving Participation Rates and Bonus payments if a PCP stops actively participating or terminates their agreement with the ACHN they originally signed with?
answer: The PCP Group must sign another agreement to actively participate with a different ACHN.

citations.quote: If a PCP stops actively participating or terminates their agreement with the ACHN they signed the original agreement with, then the PCP Group must sign another agreement to actively participate with a different ACHN to continue receiving Participation Rates and Bonus payments.

question: According to section 40.8 PCP Group Responsibilities, Functions, and Duties, within how many days must a PCP Group transfer a recipient's medical record to the receiving PCP Group upon request and authorization?
answer: Within thirty (30) days of the date of the request.

citations.quote: Transfer the recipient medical record to the receiving PCP Group at the request of the new PCP Group and as authorized by the recipient within thirty (30) days of the date of the request.

question: How much advance notice must a PCP Group provide to the Agency for disenrollment, change in practice site, Medicaid Group Billing ID, or NPI changes?
answer: At least thirty (30) days prior notice.

citations.quote: Provide the Agency with at least thirty (30) days prior notice of PCP Group disenrollment, change in practice site, Medicaid Group Billing ID, or NPI changes to allow for notification to recipients.

question: Within what drive time must a PCP Group maintain hospital admitting privileges or a formal inpatient arrangement?
answer: Forty-five (45) minutes’ drive time from the PCP Group’s practice.

citations.quote: Admitting privileges or the formal arrangement for inpatient hospital care must be maintained at a hospital that is within a forty-five (45) minutes’ drive time from the PCP Group’s practice.

question: When a patient is in the office, how quickly must the PCP or office staff assist the patient in making an EPSDT screening appointment with the Screener?
answer: Within ten (10) days.

citations.quote: If the patient is in the office, the physician/office staff will assist the patient in making a screening appointment with the Screener within ten (10) days.

question: According to Alabama Coordinated Health Network PCP office wait time standards, within what time must a scheduled appointment be seen?
answer: Within one hour.

citations.quote: • Scheduled appointment – within one hour

question: What must PCP Groups tell each new recipient about emergency room use?
answer: The requirement that the recipient must contact the PCP Group before going to the emergency room unless the recipient feels that his/her life or health is in immediate danger.

citations.quote: The requirement that the recipient must contact the PCP Group before going to the emergency room unless the recipient feels that his/her life or health is in immediate danger

question: For Alabama Coordinated Health Network Primary Care Physician and ACHN Entities billing, is BMI required for telemedicine visits?
answer: Yes. BMI will be required for all visits including the telemedicine visits.

citations.quote: Alabama Coordinated Health Network (ACHN) Primary Care Physician (PCP) and ACHN Entities Billing The BMI will be required for all visits including the telemedicine visits.

question: For Alabama Coordinated Health Network Primary Care Physician billing, which ICD-10 diagnosis code for BMI must be reported on the CMS 1500 claim form for a recipient age 20 or older with a BMI of 20.0-20.9?
answer: Z6820 Body Mass Index (BMI) 20.0-20.9, Adult
