Z6820 Body Mass Index (BMI) 20.0-20.9,

question: Within how many days of the date of service must a BMI override request and claim form be mailed to the Network Provider Assistance Unit?
answer: An Override Request Form and a clean Red Drop Ink claim form must be submitted by mail within 90 days of the date of service.

citations.quote: An Override Request Form and a clean Red Drop Ink claim form (CMS Form 1450 (UB-04) or CMS Form 1500) must be submitted to the Network Provider Assistance Unit by mail within 90 days of the date of service.

question: When are ACHN Bonus Payments made under the PCP and ACHN Entities Billing policy?
answer: Bonus payments will be made on the second or third checkwrite of the 1st month of the quarter (January, April, July, and October) unless otherwise noted.

citations.quote: NOTE: Bonus payments will be made on the second or third checkwrite of the 1st month of the quarter (January, April, July, and October) unless otherwise noted.

question: How often are Active Participation requirements monitored by the Agency and the ACHN under section 40.18?
answer: Monthly

citations.quote: Active Participation requirements will be monitored monthly by the Agency and the ACHN.

question: How frequently is the ACHN attribution report issued to providers?
answer: Quarterly after the attribution process is complete.

citations.quote: The report is produced quarterly after the attribution process is complete.

question: Under section 40.19.2 Reconsideration of Attribution, when may a PCP Group request the Medicaid Agency to reconsider its attribution calculation?
answer: A PCP Group may request reconsideration if it believes the Medicaid Agency has not properly attributed one or more Medicaid recipients to the PCP Group.

citations.quote: If a PCP Group believes the Medicaid Agency has not properly attributed one or more Medicaid recipients to the PCP Group, it may request the Medicaid Agency reconsider its attribution calculation.

question: When will the Agency distribute any remaining reserve funds to actively participating ACHN PCP groups?
answer: During the last quarter of the fiscal year.

citations.quote: During the last quarter of the fiscal year, the Agency will distribute any remaining reserve funds to actively participating ACHN PCP groups.

question: By what date and time must PCP groups submit the PCMH Recognition bonus payment attestation and proof to Medicaid?
answer: No later than October 1 by 5:00 P.M. CST annually.

citations.quote: The PCMH Recognition bonus payment attestation and proof of (achievement or progress towards achievement) are due to Medicaid annually, no later than the deadline date/time of October 1, by 5:00 P.M. (CST).

question: What must NCQA PCP groups have completed to demonstrate adequate progress towards PCMH Recognition?
answer: NCQA PCP groups must have completed at least 1 check-in and met 1 or more Cores within the qualifying timeline for the upcoming fiscal year, with proof of supporting documentation showing continued progress until full PCMH Recognition is obtained.

citations.quote: National Committee for Quality Assurance (NCQA)- PCP groups must have completed at least 1 (one) check-in and met 1 or more Cores within the qualifying timeline for the upcoming fiscal year. Core met proof of supporting documentation must show continued progress until full PCMH Recognition has been obtained.

question: What is the Profile Report (Profiler) for Alabama Coordinated Health Network providers?
answer: The Profile Report (Profiler) is the scorecard for providers to easily determine why they receive or did not receive quality bonus payments.

citations.quote: 40.21 The Profile Report The Profile Report (Profiler) is the scorecard for providers to easily determine why they receive or did not receive quality bonus payments.

question: Do certified emergency services in outpatient emergency room settings require referral or prior authorization by the PCP under the ACHN Program?
answer: No. Access to certified emergency services will not be restricted by the ACHN Program, and certified emergencies in outpatient emergency room settings do not require referral or prior authorization by the PCP, though documentation should be maintained to support emergency certification.

citations.quote: 40.25 Emergency Services Access to certified emergency services will not be restricted by the ACHN Program. Certified emergencies in outpatient emergency room settings do not require referral or prior authorization by the PCP. However, documentation should be maintained by the provider of service to support emergency certification.

question: How can providers obtain educational materials according to section 40.29?
answer: Providers may obtain educational materials using the online ordering form on the Agency’s website at www.medicaid.alabama.gov; a catalog listing these materials is also on the website.

citations.quote: NOTE: Educational materials are also available for use by providers and may be obtained using the online ordering form on the Agency’s website at www.medicaid.alabama.gov.

question: Under enrollment policies, on what basis is a PCCM-e prohibited from discriminating against recipients?
answer: A PCCM-e must not discriminate against recipients on the basis of health status or need for health care services, including termination of enrollment or refusal to reenroll except as permitted under the contract.

citations.quote: The PCCM-e must not, on the basis of health status or need for health care services, discriminate against recipients. This includes but is not limited to, termination of enrollment or refusal to reenroll a recipient except as permitted under this contract, or any practice that would reasonably be expected to discourage enrollment or reenrollment by recipients whose medical condition or history indicates probable need for substantial future medical services.

question: May a PCCM-e request disenrollment because of an adverse change in a recipient's health status?
answer: No. The PCCM-e may not request disenrollment because of an adverse change in the recipient's health status, the recipient’s utilization of medical services, the recipient’s diminished mental capacity, or the recipient’s uncooperative or disruptive behavior resulting from his or her special needs.

citations.quote: The PCCM-e may not request disenrollment because of: • An adverse change in the recipient's health status; • The recipient’s utilization of medical services; • The recipient’s diminished mental capacity; or • The recipient’s uncooperative or disruptive behavior resulting from his or her special needs (except when his or her continued enrollment seriously impairs the PCCM-e’s ability to furnish services to the recipient or other recipients).

question: What is the latest effective date for an approved disenrollment request under the ACHN Primary Care Physician PCCM-e policy?
answer: The effective date of an approved disenrollment must be no later than the first day of the second month following the month in which the recipient requests disenrollment or the PCCM-e refers the request to the Agency.

citations.quote: The effective date of an approved disenrollment must be no later than the first day of the second month following the month in which the recipient requests disenrollment or the PCCM-e refers the request to the Agency.

question: How many calendar days prior to a routine appointment must a PCCM-e establish recipient eligibility for date of service to ensure transportation is provided for Medicaid covered services?
answer: Five calendar days prior to appointments.

citations.quote: Establish recipient’s eligibility for date of service five (5) calendar days prior to appointments or within twenty-four (24) hours after urgent care appointments to ensure transportation is provided for Medicaid covered services only;

question: According to the July 2026 ACHN billing guidance, what five components must a recipient's comprehensive care plan contain?
answer: The recipient's comprehensive care plan shall be current and contain the assessment of identified needs, goals, interventions, rationales, and evaluations.

citations.quote: The recipient’s comprehensive care plan shall be current and contain five components: the assessment of identified needs, goals, interventions, rationales, and evaluations.

question: Which groups of eligible Medicaid recipients shall be included for care management services under the ACHN Program?
answer: Medically complex recipients; Maternity care recipients; Children under age 19; Parents or other caretaker relatives (POCR); Foster children; Former Foster Care; Breast and Cervical Cancer; and American Indians (note: may opt-out at any time).

citations.quote: The following groups of eligible Medicaid recipients shall be included for care management services under the ACHN Program: • Medically complex recipients • Maternity care recipients • Children under age 19; • Parents or other caretaker relatives (POCR); • Foster children; • Former Foster Care; • Breast and Cervical Cancer; and • American Indians (note: may opt-out at any time).

question: For how long after the end of pregnancy does the Agency extend postpartum coverage for pregnant recipients?
answer: Twelve (12) months after end of pregnancy.

citations.quote: The Agency extended postpartum coverage to twelve (12) months after end of pregnancy for pregnant recipients.

question: What is the basis for the training that PCCM-e must provide to staff who provide Care Management services to the Medically Complex Population?
answer: The training is based on modules produced by The National Center of Care Coordination Technical Assistance.

citations.quote: The PCCM-e shall provide training for staff providing Care Management services to the Medically Complex Population. The basis of this training will be modules produced by The National Center of Care Coordination Technical Assistance.

question: Which ACHN recipient categories must be stratified as high?
answer: Maternity for the first three months of pregnancy or initial enrollment; and Medically complex for the first three months of eligible diagnosis(es)/conditions or initial enrollment or engagement.

citations.quote: However, the recipients within the categories below must be stratified as high: • Maternity for the first three months of pregnancy or initial enrollment; and • Medically complex for the first three (3) months of eligible diagnosis(es)/conditions or initial enrollment or engagement

question: Within how many calendar days must recipient signatures for virtual encounters be obtained?
answer: Recipient signatures for virtual encounters must be attained within seven calendar days of the encounter.

citations.quote: Recipient signatures for virtual encounters must be attained within seven calendar days of the encounter.

question: Are ACHN Primary Care Physician and ACHN Entity encounters billed for F2F or virtual visits when the recipient is not in attendance eligible for payment?
answer: No. Encounters that require the recipient to attend F2F or virtually for which the recipient is not in attendance are not eligible for payment, and payments made in error are subject to recoupment.

citations.quote: Alabama Coordinated Health Network (ACHN) Primary Care Physician (PCP) and ACHN Entities Billing Encounters that require the recipient to attend F2F or virtually, for which the recipient is not in attendance, are not eligible for payment. Payments made in error are subject to recoupment.

question: Under Alabama Coordinated Health Network electronic records requirements, what must be visible on a hard copy generated from an electronic record?
answer: The recipient’s name and at a minimum date of birth or Medicaid Id number must be visible.

citations.quote: When a hard copy is generated from an electronic record the recipient’s name and at a minimum date of birth or Medicaid Id number must be visible.

question: Which authentication methods are acceptable for entries in a recipient's record under Alabama Coordinated Health Network billing rules, and which is not acceptable?
answer: Acceptable authentication is handwritten signatures, written initials for treatment plan reviews, or computer entry associated with electronic records — not a typed signature. A stamped signature is not acceptable.

citations.quote: Authentication may include handwritten signatures, written initials (for treatment plan reviews), or computer entry (associated with electronic records—not a typed signature). A stamped signature is not acceptable.

question: According to the July 2026 ACHN manual, what criteria must recipient goals in a care plan meet?
answer: The recipient’s goals should be SMART Goals: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time based.

citations.quote: The recipient’s goals should be SMART Goals: • Specific, • Measurable, • Achievable, • Relevant, • and Time based.

question: According to the Alabama Medicaid July 2026 ACHN PCP manual, what goal status documentation is required during care plan evaluation?
answer: Care management staff must document the status of each goal as met, unmet, or in progress along with a summary of what was (un)accomplished and why.

citations.quote: Documentation shall include the status of each goal i.e., met, unmet, or in progress along with a summary what was (un)accomplished and why.

question: If a recipient chooses not to attend an MCT meeting prior to the meeting being scheduled, what documentation and approval are required for payment eligibility?
answer: The PCCM-e must maintain attestation documentation within the HIMS to support the refusal, and Agency approval is needed prior to payment. This approval must be granted prior to the meeting being conducted.

citations.quote: If the recipient chooses to not attend prior to the meeting being scheduled, the PCCM-e must maintain attestation documentation within the HIMS to support the refusal. In these instances, Agency approval will be needed prior to payment. This approval must be granted prior to the meeting being conducted.

question: How much advance written notice must a PCCM-e give a recipient about the date, time, location, and purpose of an MCT meeting, and what follow-up is required if the initial notification is telephonic?
answer: The PCCM-e shall notify the recipient in writing of the date, time, location, and purpose of the MCT at least 10 business days before the recipient’s MCT meeting. Telephonic notification is permitted but must be followed up with a written recipient MCT meeting notification letter via postal service.

citations.quote: The PCCM-e shall notify the recipient, in writing, of the date, time, location, and purpose of the MCT at least 10 business days before the date of the recipient’s MCT meeting. The notification can be telephonic but must be followed-up with a written recipient MCT meeting notification letter via postal service.

question: According to the Alabama Coordinated Health Network PCP billing guidelines, what are the composition requirements for a valid MCT meeting?
answer: To be considered a valid MCT meeting, the meeting shall consist of any three of the six disciplines/professionals based on the recipient’s needs. At least one of the three disciplines must be the recipient’s PCP or appropriate PCP representative. The recipient, his or her family member, or caregiver cannot be counted as one of the three levels of disciplines.

citations.quote: To be considered a valid MCT meeting, the meeting shall consist of any three of the six disciplines/ professionals based on the recipient’s needs. At least one of the three disciplines must be the recipient’s PCP or appropriate PCP representative. The recipient, his or her family member, or caregiver cannot be counted as one of the three levels of disciplines.

question: What hours must the PCCM-e toll-free recipient services telephone line be available on Business Days?
answer: 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. CT on Business Days.

citations.quote: This line shall be available on Business Days, between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. CT (central time).

question: According to Alabama Coordinated Health Network section 40, what minimum emergency information must the automated system provide callers with operating instructions on what to do in case of an emergency?
answer: The automated system must include what constitutes an Emergency Medical Condition and Emergency Services, and the fact that the recipient has a right to use any hospital or other setting for emergency care, in accordance with 42 C.F.R. § 438.10(g)(2)(v).

citations.quote: This automated system must provide callers with operating instructions on what to do in case of an emergency which must include, at a minimum, the following information in accordance with 42 C.F.R. § 438.10(g)(2)(v): • What constitutes an Emergency Medical Condition and Emergency Services; and • The fact that the recipient has a right to use any hospital or other setting for emergency care.

question: What phone number should a provider call for general ACHN billing questions or to request an application package?

citations.quote: Alabama Coordinated Health Network (ACHN) Primary Care Physician (PCP) and ACHN Entities Billing 40.48 Contact Information Summary For general ACHN billing questions or to request an application package, call the Provider Assistance Center: 1 (800) 688-7989.

question: What referral is required before an Alabama Medicaid enrolled NFP entity can submit for reimbursement for services rendered to Alabama Medicaid recipients?
answer: Referral by an Alabama Coordinated Health Network (ACHN) provider of an eligible Medicaid recipient to an Alabama Medicaid enrolled NFP entity is required before the NFP entity submits for reimbursement to the Agency.

citations.quote: Referral by an Alabama Coordinated Health Network (ACHN) provider of an eligible Medicaid recipient to an Alabama Medicaid enrolled NFP entity is required. This referral is needed before the NFP entity submits for reimbursement to the Agency for services rendered to Alabama Medicaid recipients.

question: Will Alabama Medicaid separately reimburse direct care services such as wound care provided by an NFP nurse during an NFP case management visit?
answer: No. Medicaid will not separately reimburse for any direct care services, such as wound care, rendered by an NFP nurse in the course of their NFP case management visit.

citations.quote: 41.2.2 Limitations Medicaid will not separately reimburse for any direct care services, such as wound care, rendered by an NFP nurse in the course of their NFP case management visit.

question: According to Alabama Medicaid NFP documentation requirements, is a stamped signature acceptable for entries?
answer: No. The author must personally or electronically sign each entry; a stamped signature is not acceptable.

citations.quote: Additionally, the author of each entry must either, personally or electronically sign his or her entry. A stamped signature is not acceptable.

question: Under 41.3.3 Signatures for Nurse-Family Partnership, what must the Home Visiting Nurse obtain and keep on file to verify recipient presence for face-to-face encounters?
answer: The Home Visiting Nurse must obtain a handwritten signature to be kept on file on the home visit form as verification that the recipient was present on the date of service for which the provider seeks payment for face-to-face encounters. If payment is made on claims for which a signature is not available and the Agency accepted expectation is not applicable, the funds paid to the provider covering the claim will be recouped.

citations.quote: The Home Visiting Nurse must obtain a handwritten signature to be kept on file, (the home visit form) as verification that the recipient was present on the date of service for which the provider seeks payment for face-to face encounters.

When payment has been made on claims for which a signature is not available and of the Agency accepted expectation is not applicable, the funds paid to the provider covering the claim will be recouped.

question: Under Nurse-Family Partnership 41.3.5, are journal notes sufficient documentation for telehealth encounters and/or eligibility verification?
answer: No. Journal notes are not sufficient documentation for telehealth encounters and/or eligibility verification, though they can be submitted to document brief interactions such as phone calls, referral updates, missed appointments, or late entry notes.

citations.quote: Journal notes are not sufficient documentation for telehealth encounters and /or eligibility verification.
Journal notes can be submitted to document brief interactions between the home visiting nurse and the recipient.

question: According to the Nurse-Family Partnership section, what criteria should recipient goals meet?
answer: Recipient goals should be SMART Goals: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time based.

citations.quote: The recipient’s goals should be SMART Goals: • Specific, • Measurable, • Achievable, • Relevant, • and Time based.

question: How many visits per month are expected for Nurse-Family Partnership reimbursement, and what modifier must be appended to visits beyond the first?
answer: At least two visits per month with the recipient are expected, and all visits beyond the first must be filed with an XE modifier appended to the corresponding NFP service, e.g., T2023 HD U1 XE.

citations.quote: However, it is expected that at least two visits per month with the recipient will occur and there must be documentation in the recipient’s record for each visit performed.
All visits beyond the first must be filed with an XE modifier appended to the corresponding NFP service (e.g., T2023 HD U1 XE).

question: Which diagnosis code must Nurse-Family Partnership providers include on each Medicaid claim?
answer: Z71.9 (counseling, unspecified)

citations.quote: NFP providers must include the following information on the claim:
The Z71.9 (counseling, unspecified) diagnosis code

question: What diagnosis code must be included on Nurse-Family Partnership claims submitted to Alabama Medicaid with dates of service on or after April 1, 2023?

question: Under Alabama Medicaid, when may a recipient receive another Mirena IUD within a 5-year period?

citations.quote: NOTE: Effective 1/1/2010, the Mirena IUD is restricted to 1 every 5 years.

The only exception to this 5 year restriction is if the recipient meets one or more of the criteria listed below. If a recipient meets one or more of the criteria listed below she may qualify for another Mirena IUD within a 5 year period.
1. Recipient develops high blood pressure or any other medical condition that would allow for a progestin only method.
2. Any nulliparous woman who has a spontaneous expulsion within 6 months of placement.
3. Mirena IUD is removed to allow a pregnancy. Once delivered, recipient is eligible for another Mirena IUD.
4. Surgical removal of an embedded IUD in an office or outpatient setting.

question: What is the Automated Voice Response System (AVRS) according to the Alabama Medicaid Glossary of Terms?
answer: The automated voice information system available 24 hours a day to Medicaid providers for inquiries of recipient eligibility, lock-in, other insurance, last check information, National Drug Code (NDC) information, procedure code pricing, claim statistics, and PA information.

citations.quote: Automated Voice Response The automated voice information system available 24 hours a day to System (AVRS) Medicaid providers for inquiries of recipient eligibility, lock-in, other insurance, last check information, National Drug Code (NDC) information, procedure code pricing, claim statistics, and PA information.

question: According to the Alabama Medicaid Glossary of Terms July 2026, what distinguishing characteristic separates copayments from coinsurance?
answer: Copayments are flat or variable dollar amounts and coinsurance is a defined percentage of the charges for services rendered.

citations.quote: Some copayments are referred to as coinsurance, with the distinguishing characteristics that copayments are flat or variable dollar amounts and coinsurance is a defined percentage of the charges for services rendered.

question: According to the July 2026 Alabama Medicaid Glossary of Terms, what is an Edit?

question: According to the Alabama Medicaid Glossary of Terms, what is generic substitution?

question: According to the Alabama Medicaid Glossary of Terms on page 9, how is an Inpatient defined?

question: According to the Alabama Medicaid Glossary of Terms, what are examples of medical supplies?

question: According to the Alabama Medicaid Glossary of Terms, what is required for Medicaid reimbursement of an over-the-counter drug?
answer: Medicaid reimbursement for an over-the-counter drug requires a prescription, even though OTC drugs are available to the public without a prescription.

question: What is the definition of per diem according to the Alabama Medicaid Glossary of Terms?
answer: Literally, per day. Term that is applied to determining costs for a day of care and is an average that does not reflect true cost for each patient.

question: According to the Alabama Medicaid Glossary of Terms, what is Prior Authorization?
answer: Approval provided by Medicaid for specified services for a specific recipient to a specific provider, or the process of obtaining prior approval as to the appropriateness of the service or medication. Prior authorization does not guarantee coverage.

question: What is the maximum amount an eligible 340B entity, other than a disproportionate share hospital, children’s hospital excluded from Medicare PPS, free-standing cancer hospital exempt from Medicare PPS, sole community hospital, rural referral center, or critical access hospital, may bill Alabama Medicaid for a drug purchased by or on behalf of a Medicaid recipient?
answer: The amount billed shall not exceed the entity's actual acquisition cost for the drug, as charged by the manufacturer at a price consistent with the Veterans Health Care Act of 1992, plus the dispensing fee established by the Medicaid Agency.

question: According to Alabama Medicaid Appendix H, how are billing units calculated for procedure code 95165 and what is the NCCI maximum?
answer: Reimbursement for procedure code 95165 is based on preparing a vial containing a mixture of all appropriate antigens plus diluents, with one cc equal to one billing unit. The National Correct Coding Initiative sets the maximum number of billable units for procedure code 95165 at 30, i.e., three 10cc vials.

citations.quote: The reimbursement for procedure code 95165 is based on preparing a vial containing a mixture of all the appropriate antigens plus diluents and calculating the billing units in the vial. Therefore, one (1) cc equals one (1) billing unit.
The maximum number of billable units (three-10cc vials) for procedure code 95165 was set as “30” by the National Correct Coding Initiative (NCCI).

question: What billing requirements apply to a claim for procedure codes E1399 or E1399 (EP) under Appendix P?
answer: The procedure code must be entered on the claim as one line item, the units billed must be entered as “1” unit, and the dollar amount billed must be the total dollar amount for all items approved on the prior authorization for the date of service on the claim, combined as one lump sum. If each approved item is billed on separate lines or more than one unit is billed for the same dates of service, the claim will be denied.

citations.quote: NOTE: To file a claim for procedure codes E1399 or E1399 (EP): 1. The procedure code must be entered on the claim as one line item. 2. The units billed must be entered as “1” unit. 3. The dollar amount billed must be the “total” dollar amount for all items approved on the prior authorization for the date of service on the claim.

In other words, the money amounts for multiple items approved on a prior authorization request for E1399 or E1399 (EP) must be combined and the total money amount must be billed as one lump sum. The total units for all items must be billed as “one” unit. If each approved item for E1399 or E1399 (EP) is billed on separate lines or if more than one unit is billed, for the same dates of service, the claim will be denied.
